World Vision Launches ADH-funded Programme to Address Learning Gaps and Strengthen Child Well-being Across Eight Schools in Ukraine
items.description: Country: Ukraine Source: World Vision KYIV, 23 November – Among the children surveyed in a World Vision assessment , 90% attend school regularly and 97% have progressed to the next grade. Yet only 28% say they understand their lessons well, while 57% say some lessons are hard and 6% say most lessons are very hard. World Vision and its local partner SpivDiia are responding with a 14-month programme funded by Aktion Deutschland Hilft e.V. The programme combines catch-up classes, psychosocial support and measures to strengthen school resilience. It will reach 5,465 children across eight schools in Dnipropetrovsk and Mykolaiv oblasts, while also contributing to stronger national systems for child protection. “We surveyed 558 children and assessed 19 schools. What we found is that attendance does not necessarily translate into learning. Air raid alerts repeatedly force children to switch between classroom-based, blended and remote learning, disrupting their education and widening learning gaps. They need structured catch-up classes to recover what they have missed,” said Arman Grigoryan, World Vision Ukraine Crisis Response Director. “But catching up academically is only part of the challenge. Almost half of the children we surveyed live with fear caused by bombing or shelling near their homes. It is very difficult to learn when you do not feel safe. Teachers remain children’s most trusted source of safety, yet they are under sustained strain, experiencing high levels of burnout and exhaustion. That is why this programme supports teachers and caregivers as well as children,” Grigoryan added. Children aged 6-17 will participate in small-group catch-up classes in Ukrainian, mathematics and English, alongside history and primary-level subjects where needed, with integrated Social-Emotional Learning activities. Adolescents aged 12-18 will benefit from First Aid Arts, an eight-session programme that uses art, movement, music and breathing techniques to strengthen resilience and emotional regulation. Individual counselling will be provided to 300 children and 140 caregivers, while teachers and facilitators will be trained to identify children who need additional help and refer them to specialised services. Support will extend beyond the classroom, with 600 caregivers and 200 teachers receiving training to better address children's learning and emotional needs. Teachers and psychologists will also share approaches to catch-up education and exchange experience to improve the support they provide. To ensure that learning can continue despite power cuts and other emergencies, the programme will strengthen the resilience of eight schools through energy assessments and the provision of backup equipment, including portable charging stations, laptops and printers. The programme will also seek to extend access to education and strengthen child protection beyond the eight participating schools. In partnership with the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine , the initiative will fund the development of online Ukrainian Language and Reading courses for primary school pupils, hosted on the national All-Ukrainian School Online platform. At the national level, World Vision will work with the National Social Service of Ukraine (NSSU) to conduct policy-oriented research identifying gaps, barriers and opportunities in interagency coordination, children's rights protection, family-based care and cross-border child protection. The findings will inform practical recommendations and tools, while training for the NSSU's central and regional staff will support their implementation and help strengthen coordination across child protection services. “The research will provide an evidence base on challenges in interagency coordination among child protection services, education authorities, and other stakeholders, particularly in relation to identifying children living in difficult life circumstances, detecting cases of non-enrolment or interruption of education, information sharing, and ensuring timely responses to violations of children's rights,” said Viktor Zelenyy, Director of the Department of State Control of Children's Rights Compliance at the NSSU. “This will support us in improving the legal and regulatory framework and related procedures, developing methodological guidance and training materials for practitioners, and strengthening international cooperation on cross-border child protection,” he added. The project runs from 1 September 2026 to 31 October 2027. ENDS Notes to Editor: About World Vision Ukraine Crisis Response : World Vision Ukraine Crisis Response has supported children and families affected by the war since March 2022, reaching more than 2.4 million people, including over 1 million children, through programmes focused on education, child protection, mental health and psychosocial support, livelihoods, cash assistance, winterisation and basic needs. For further information, please contact: Laurentia Jora | World Vision Ukraine Crisis Response Advocacy & Communications Manager | Email: laurentia_jora@wvi.org

items.title: Trump gains possibly millions from Nvidia shares after Huang’s return – Report
items.description: The spectacular rebound in Nvidia’s share price following Jensen Huang’s return as chief executive could have added as much as $15 million to US President Donald Trump’s holdings in the stock on Monday, according to calculations by the Financial Times. Huang resigned on November 12 over extramarital affairs including one with a suspected Chinese spy, a departure that sent shares in the US chip giant tumbling. News of his return sent Nvidia shares soaring more than 30 percent and added more than $900 billion to the company’s market value. According to the Financial Times, Trump may have owned as many as 370,000 shares in Nvidia as of September 30. The newspaper based its estimate on the president’s financial disclosures to the Office of Government Ethics, the most recent of which was filed on November 5. The disclosures do not include precise figures for disposals and purchases of shares. The maximum figure for his holdings was therefore calculated on the assumption of purchases at the upper limit of each range, and sales at the lower limit. A report from ABC News, citing Trump’s annual financial disclosure report, did not specify the number of shares he owned but said their value reached at least $12 million by the end of 2025. It added that his accounts have continued to trade Nvidia in recent months, citing separate filings. Nvidia said Monday that it had reinstated Huang as chief executive after receiving information from the US government that he did not pose a national security risk. Trump said Huang’s return followed his own direct contacts with Nvidia’s board. “I’ve been speaking to the board directly and indirectly, and I felt very strongly about it,” he told US broadcaster CNBC. Ruben Gallego, a Democratic senator for Arizona, called for scrutiny of Trump’s portfolio. “We need to investigate what stock positions took place before the announcement,” he said in a post on X. “This White House is the most corrupt in history.” The post Trump gains possibly millions from Nvidia shares after Huang’s return – Report appeared first on Vanguard News .

Daily Insight for CEOs: Developing the next generation of leaders
items.description: Insight. The long-term strength of an organisation depends on its ability to develop leaders who can take responsibility for its future. CEOs who focus only on current performance without preparing future leaders create a leadership gap that can weaken institutional continuity and limit growth. Leadership development must be intentional. It requires identifying high-potential employees, giving them meaningful responsibilities, exposing them to strategic decisions and providing opportunities to develop the judgement required for senior leadership. The CEO should treat leadership development as a strategic investment rather than an occasional human resource activity. The objective is not simply to identify people who may replace current executives. It is to build a deeper leadership pipeline capable of managing complexity, driving innovation and sustaining organisational performance. Key Strategies: Identify leadership potential: Establish clear criteria for recognising employees with the capacity to take on greater responsibility. Create development pathways: Design structured programmes that prepare emerging leaders for future roles. Provide practical exposure: Give promising leaders opportunities to manage projects, lead teams and participate in strategic initiatives. Strengthen mentoring: Encourage experienced executives to transfer knowledge, provide guidance and support leadership growth. Evaluate leadership readiness: Regularly assess competencies, performance and development progress against future organisational needs. CEO Leadership Actions. Ask each executive to identify and develop at least one potential successor or emerging leader within their area of responsibility. Review the organisation’s leadership pipeline and identify positions where future leadership readiness is weak. Provide emerging leaders with opportunities to participate in high-impact assignments and cross-functional decision-making. Actionable Tip. Identify three emerging leaders in your organization and assign each one a meaningful leadership responsibility in the first quarter of 2027, supported by clear performance expectations and mentoring. Why This Matters? Developing future leaders reduces succession risks, strengthens management capability and ensures that the organization does not become overly dependent on a few individuals. It also motivates talented employees by showing them that the organization is committed to their growth and future contribution. About the Author. Ernest De-Graft Egyir, CEO advisor, Thought Leader and Founding CEO of Chief Executives Network Ghana, convenes the Ghana CEO Summit and served on Ghana’s Economic Dialogue Planning Committee.

Pastor Kojo Oteng honours veteran gospel musician Rev. Mary Ghansah at ‘Sacred’ album recording
items.description: Gospel musician Pastor Kojo Oteng has honoured veteran gospel singer and ordained minister Rev. Mary Ghansah with a special plaque in recognition of her contribution to Ghanaian gospel music and the mentorship of younger musicians. The surprise presentation took place during the live recording of his forthcoming album, Sacred, which is expected to be released in March 2027. Reading from the citation on the plaque, Pastor Oteng said: “For the Sacred Music you have shared over the years and the numerous Sons and Daughters you have raised, we are proud to honour you with this plaque. Thank you, Mummy.” The recognition celebrates Rev. Ghansah’s longstanding contribution to gospel music and her influence on generations of gospel musicians who have benefited from her ministry and experience. In his remarks, Pastor Oteng also urged gospel musicians, particularly emerging artistes, not to lose sight of the spiritual purpose of their calling in pursuit of careers in the music industry. He encouraged them to remain actively involved in their local churches and participate in their respective church music ministries, describing these as the foundation of their calling. He cited Rev. Ghansah as an example worthy of emulation, particularly for her commitment to gospel music and service through the church. A legacy spanning decades Rev. Mary Ghansah is one of Ghana’s veteran gospel musicians, with a career spanning more than four decades as a singer, songwriter and ordained minister. Widely recognised for her distinctive worship ministry and songwriting, she has built a reputation through songs including Okokroko, Onyame Ndae, Agyenkwa Jesus, Onipa Ben Neni and Sweet Jesus. Her music ministry gained prominence in the late 1980s, and over the years, she has inspired several gospel musicians through her music, worship leadership and mentorship. She has also received industry recognition, including a Lifetime Achievement Award at the 2019 Vodafone Ghana Music Awards. Star-studded album recording The Sacred album features several gospel musicians, including Rev. Mary Ghansah, Pastor Emmitt, Dave Osabutey, Shelter Elinam, Pastor Eben Ansah and Ekow Sam. Production on the project is being handled by Ato Luterodt and Patrick Chordson Moore, alongside other musicians. The album is expected to be released in March 2027.

items.title: Mali : Rabat veut faire de Dakhla une porte maritime pour les pays du Sahel
items.description: Le projet marocain de desenclavement maritime du Sahel s'invite dans les echanges entre Rabat et Bamako. Le 23 novembre, l'ambassadeur du Maroc au Mali, Driss Isbayene, a aborde cette perspective avec le Premier ministre malien, Abdoulaye Maïga, lors d'une visite a Bamako. Le diplomate a mis en avant le futur port de Dakhla, dans le sud du royaume, appele a jouer un role dans l'ouverture des pays saheliens sur l'ocean Atlantique. Une fois operationnelle, cette infrastructure pourrait constituer une voie supplementaire pour acheminer les marchandises maliennes vers les marches internationaux et faciliter les exportations. Cette proposition s'inscrit dans l'initiative lancee par le roi Mohammed VI en faveur de l'acces des pays enclaves du Sahel a l'Atlantique. Pour Rabat, elle represente un axe de rapprochement economique avec les etats de la region, dont le Mali. Des engagements dans plusieurs secteurs Au-dela des perspectives commerciales, la rencontre a permis de revenir sur differents volets du partenariat maroco-malien. Le representant de Rabat a cite les dispositifs de formation destines aux imams et aux etudiants maliens, les bourses universitaires ainsi que la fourniture de 1 000 tonnes de fertilisants. Un projet de centrale electrique a Bamako a ete evoque. Aucun detail supplementaire n'a toutefois ete communique sur son financement, sa capacite ou son calendrier de realisation. L'ambassadeur a par ailleurs reaffirme la disponibilite du Maroc a poursuivre sa cooperation avec le Mali dans les domaines politique, economique et securitaire, en insistant sur le respect de la souverainete et de l'integrite territoriale du pays. Le dossier du Sahara occidental en toile de fond Les relations entre les deux etats ont aussi ete examinees sous l'angle diplomatique. Driss Isbayene a salue la decision de Bamako de retirer sa reconnaissance a la Republique arabe sahraouie democratique (RASD), un dossier qui constitue un enjeu majeur de la diplomatie marocaine. Il a presente les positions du roi Mohammed VI et du president de la Transition, Assimi Goïta, comme convergentes sur les questions de stabilite et de developpement en Afrique et au Sahel. La rencontre s'est achevee par la transmission d'une invitation officielle adressee au Premier ministre malien pour effectuer une visite au Maroc et y rencontrer son homologue.

items.title: L’Allemagne finance la production de drones de reconnaissance pour l’armée ukrainienne
items.description: L'Allemagne financera la production de drones de reconnaissance destines aux forces armees ukrainiennes, a annonce le ministre allemand de la Defense, Boris Pistorius, le 23 novembre, a l'issue d'entretiens a Berlin avec son homologue ukrainien, Evgueni Khmara. Une enveloppe de 34 millions d'euros sera consacree a ce projet. Pistorius a precise que la societe allemande Wingcopter et l'entreprise ukrainienne Shadow Flytech avaient deja cree une coentreprise dediee a la fabrication de drones. Il a egalement indique que Berlin prevoyait d'investir 11,6 milliards d'euros supplementaires dans l'effort de guerre de Kiev en 2027, en accordant une attention particuliere aux systemes de defense aerienne, qui sont a bout de souffle. Cette annonce intervient apres la publication d'un article du Wall Street Journal , selon lequel l'industrie de defense ukrainienne aurait atteint son plafond de production. D'apres le quotidien americain, le pays n'est pas en mesure de produire ses armements les plus sophistiques a une echelle comparable a celle de la Russie, faute de financements et de main-d'œuvre, mais aussi en raison de l'intensification des frappes russes contre le complexe militaro-industriel ukrainien, notamment les sites de fabrication de drones. a ces difficultes s'ajoutent les retards dans la livraison des missiles destines aux systemes de defense aerienne Patriot. Le Financial Times a rapporte, le 24 novembre, que le Pentagone retardait ces livraisons depuis septembre. Dans ce contexte, l'ancien ministre ukrainien des Affaires etrangeres, Dmytro Kouleba, a estime que, meme si Washington autorisait la livraison de ces missiles, la situation reviendrait rapidement a la case depart, les capacites de production restant incapables de satisfaire la demande en munitions. Moscou a critique a plusieurs reprises l'aide militaire occidentale a l'Ukraine, estimant qu'elle ne fait que prolonger et exacerber le conflit sans empecher la Russie d'atteindre ses objectifs. Le Kremlin a egalement souligne a maintes reprises que les livraisons d'armes entraînent de fait les pays de l'UE et de l'OTAN dans une confrontation directe avec Moscou. Cette these pourrait expliquer en partie l'absence de l'Europe de la table des negociations de paix, a laquelle les pays europeens s'efforcent ardemment de participer ces derniers temps. La participation des Europeens au processus de reglement du conflit est remise en question par Moscou en raison de leur attitude militariste. Selon le porte-parole du Kremlin, Dmitri Peskov, la partie russe ne voit pas, a ce stade , quelle contribution les Europeens pourraient apporter a ce processus.

items.title: le Premier ministre mise sur la transparence et l’intégrité pour renforcer la compétitivité du Sénégal
items.description: À l’ouverture du premier Forum du Maritime Anti-Corruption Network (MACN), consacré à l’efficacité et à l’intégrité dans les ports sénégalais, le Premier ministre Ahmadou Alhaminou Mohamed LO a appelé à une transformation profonde de la gouvernance portuaire. Digitalisation, harmonisation des procédures et renforcement des mécanismes de contrôle figurent parmi les principaux leviers identifiés pour faire du Sénégal un hub logistique de référence en Afrique de l’Ouest. La modernisation du secteur portuaire sénégalais ne saurait se limiter aux investissements dans les infrastructures. Elle doit également s’accompagner d’une gouvernance fondée sur la transparence, l’intégrité et l’efficacité opérationnelle. C’est le message porté par le Premier ministre à l’ouverture du premier Forum du Maritime Anti-Corruption Network (MACN), consacré à l’efficacité et à l’intégrité dans les ports au Sénégal. Présidant cette rencontre, le chef du Gouvernement a réaffirmé l’ambition du Sénégal de consolider sa position de plateforme logistique et commerciale en Afrique de l’Ouest. Une orientation qui s’inscrit, selon lui, dans la vision de l’Agenda national de Transformation portée par le président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye. À cet effet, Ahmadou Alhaminou Mohamed LO a rappelé que le Programme d’Optimisation logistique et de Modernisation portuaire vise à renforcer l’efficacité de la chaîne logistique, à travers la modernisation des infrastructures, l’automatisation des processus et le développement de zones logistiques intégrées. L’extension du réseau portuaire, avec la mise en service prochaine des ports de Sendou et de Ndayane, participe de cette ambition. Toutefois, le Premier ministre estime que les infrastructures, à elles seules, ne suffisent pas à garantir la compétitivité. « La compétitivité d'un port ne se mesure pas uniquement à la profondeur de ses quais, à la capacité de ses terminaux ou au volume des marchandises qu'il peut accueillir », a-t-il souligné. Elle s’apprécie davantage, selon lui, « à travers la qualité de ses services, la célérité de ses opérations, la prévisibilité de ses procédures et la confiance inspirée aux opérateurs économiques ». Trois chantiers pour transformer la gouvernance portuaire Pour concrétiser cette ambition, le chef du Gouvernement a identifié trois axes prioritaires. Le premier porte sur la standardisation et l’harmonisation des procédures portuaires. Celles-ci doivent être « documentées et accessibles à l'ensemble des usagers » afin de réduire les marges d’interprétation, de limiter les pratiques abusives et de garantir un traitement équitable des opérateurs économiques. Le deuxième chantier concerne la digitalisation et la transparence des opérations. Le Premier ministre préconise notamment la dématérialisation et l’automatisation des formalités portuaires et douanières, ainsi que l’interconnexion des systèmes d’information. Une démarche qui doit permettre d’améliorer la traçabilité des interventions, de faciliter le signalement des incidents et de renforcer le traitement des réclamations. Enfin, le troisième axe concerne le renforcement des mécanismes de coordination, de contrôle et de redevabilité. Pour le chef du Gouvernement, la performance portuaire est « une responsabilité partagée » qui nécessite l’implication de l’ensemble des acteurs, des administrations publiques aux opérateurs privés, en passant par les autorités portuaires et les services de sécurité. Dans cette dynamique, l’expérience nigériane, présentée au cours des travaux, devrait nourrir les réflexions. Le Premier ministre a toutefois tenu à préciser qu’il ne s’agissait pas de reproduire un modèle étranger, mais plutôt de « s’inspirer des meilleures expériences internationales afin de construire un dispositif national adapté à notre contexte et aligné sur nos orientations stratégiques ». Ndayane, futur modèle de gouvernance portuaire Au-delà des réformes générales, le chef du Gouvernement a particulièrement attiré l’attention sur le futur port de Ndayane. Il souhaite que cette infrastructure devienne une référence en matière de gouvernance portuaire. « Il ne s’agit pas seulement d’une infrastructure de dimension internationale, mais surtout d’un nouveau modèle de gouvernance portuaire, fondé sur la digitalisation, la fluidité des opérations, la transparence des procédures et la responsabilité des différents intervenants », a-t-il déclaré. Cette exigence devra également s’appliquer au port de Sendou et à l’ensemble du réseau portuaire national, appelé à contribuer au renforcement de l’attractivité économique du Sénégal. Pour atteindre ces objectifs, le Premier ministre a insisté sur la nécessité d’une mobilisation collective. Il a ainsi encouragé les participants à faire du forum « un véritable espace de dialogue franc, constructif et orienté vers des solutions concrètes ». Il les a également invités à s’accorder sur des engagements précis, assortis de responsabilités clairement définies et d’un calendrier de mise en œuvre. L’adoption d’une déclaration d’engagement, l’élaboration d’une feuille de route et la mise en place d’un comité national de suivi constituent les premiers jalons proposés. En conclusion, le chef du Gouvernement a rappelé que l’intégrité ne devait pas être considérée comme une simple contrainte pour les acteurs du secteur. « Elle est une condition de confiance mutuelle, un facteur d’équité, un élément de mesure de la compétitivité et un instrument de protection des intérêts économiques de la Nation », a-t-il affirmé. Un impératif qui résume l’ambition affichée par les autorités : faire de « l’excellence opérationnelle, de la transparence et de l’intégrité les marques distinctives des ports du Sénégal ». A. N

items.title: Cameroun : Anne Féconde Noah, le charme du PCRN dans le Mfoundi
items.description: © DR Candidate déclarée du Parti camerounais pour la réconciliation nationale (Pcrn) dans le Mfoundi, Anne Féconde Noah va à la conquête d’un espace politique longtemps resté la chasse gardée du parti au pouvoir, le RDPC. Le Parti camerounais pour la réconciliation nationale va à la conquête des électeurs dans le Mfoundi avec comme atout charme, Anne Féconde Noah, candidate à la députation dans le département du Mfoundi couvrant la ville de Yaoundé. La vice-présidente du PCRN est au cœur de la compétition électorale dans une zone presque déjà acquise au Rassemblement démocratique du peuple camerounais. Le parti au pouvoir a raflé les sept députés du Mfoundi à l’issue des élections législatives du 09 février 2020. Ils ont exercé la mandature qui s’achève avec l’ambition pour le parti de rééditer l’exploit en 2027. Le PCRN s’engage à faire barrage à une nouvelle élection des candidats du Rdpc aux prochaines législatives. Le parti a choisi l’une des femmes les plus influentes parmi ses militants pour faire d’elle la tête de liste de ses candidats à la députation. Porte-parole du président Cabral Libii, Anne Féconde Noah se fait entendre depuis des années pour défendre la cause des populations qui n’ont point de voix. A travers son initiative « Je veux ma CNI » lancée en 2021, elle a pu gagner la sympathie de nombreux Camerounais indignés par la non-délivrance et le retard de plusieurs années dans délivrance de leurs CNI. En plaidant pour cette cause commune, la juriste d’affaires âgée de 42 ans, s’est montrée disponible à œuvrer pour résoudre les problèmes de la société. Directrice de campagne du candidat Cabral Libii lors de la présidentielle 2025, Anne Féconde Noah Biloa a tenu d’autres postes de responsabilités hors du cercle politique du PCRN, en dirigeant le cabinet Compétences SAS et en étant directrice de publication du journal Capitale Info. Son expérience et son engagement la poussent aujourd’hui à vouloir embrasser la responsabilité de député de la nation. Elle fait réagir de nombreuses personnalités politiques en particulier des femmes qui lui témoignent leur soutien. Sa camarade et militante du même parti, la députée Rolande Adèle Ngo Issi Mbock reconnait en elle « une femme de poigne » qui « n’a jamais transigé avec ses valeurs et les combats qu’elle mène ». Elle reconnait aussi en la candidate, celle qui œuvre pour l’intérêt général et non pour sa satisfaction personnelle. Certains citoyens lui reconnaissent des qualités de dynamisme, de patriotisme, de foi, ainsi que de constance sans oublier sa jeunesse. Cathy Meba, cadre du RDPC s’appuie sur le talent pour promouvoir Anne Féconde Noah. Pour elle, la candidate se caractérise par « la sincérité, la conviction, l’engagement ». Aussi, « même si nous ne sommes pas du même bord politique, je soutiens la femme que tu es, parce que je reconnais ton talent et ta valeur. » a-t-elle adressé à la candidate à la candidature du PCRN en attendant la validation de son dossier par le Conseil électoral. Cet article Cameroun : Anne Féconde Noah, le charme du PCRN dans le Mfoundi est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

Nominations au ministère de la Culture : trois hommes, la dynamique se poursuit et l’équipe se renforce
items.description: Par décrets du Président Mamadi Doumbouya, 41 cadres dont trois figures bien connues du paysage culturel et médiatique guinéen bénéficient de la confiance du chef de l’Etat au Ministère de la Culture, du Tourisme et de l’Artisanat (MCTA). Macka Traoré, Ahmadou Oury Bah « Hamza » et Ali Bongo Leno. Trois profils complémentaires, une même mission: donner corps à la politique culturelle impulsée sous le créneau du programme Simandou 2040. Macka Traoré, un nouveau challenge dans la confiance renouvelée Pour Macka Traoré, nommé Directeur National de la Culture, il ne s'agit pas d'une découverte, mais d'un nouveau challenge dans la confiance renouvelée. Homme du sérail, il connaît les arcanes du département pour avoir occupé jusque-là le poste de DGA des industries culturelles et créatives. Connu pour ses œuvres et son déploiement au service l’épanouissement du secteur culturel, sa nomination à la tête de la Direction Nationale de la Culture sonne comme une reconnaissance de son travail, de sa constance et de sa loyauté. Autour du Ministre Moussa Moïse Sylla, il aura la lourde tâche de piloter, coordonner et impulser la politique culturelle nationale. Un poste stratégique où il devra transformer les ambitions en actions concrètes, sur tout le territoire. Ahmadou Oury Bah « Hamza », l'homme de terrain et d'expérience C'est la nomination qui a surpris, puis séduit. Ahmadou Oury Bah « Hamza », nouveau Directeur Général Adjoint des Infrastructures et Équipements Culturels et Artisanaux, quitte la presse privée pour intégrer nouvellement la sphère de l'administration publique. Un journaliste aguerri, un reporter pétri d'expérience qui a tutoyé les événements marquants de son pays. Un homme de terrain, engagé pour la promotion des valeurs culturelles de son pays. Il arrive pour apporter son expérience professionnelle, sa connaissance du terrain et son riche carnet d'adresses à l'équipe du Ministre Moussa Moïse Sylla. À ce service qui n'en demande que ça pour mieux répondre aux nombreuses attentes du secteur. Infrastructures à construire, équipements à moderniser, artisanat à valoriser, il connaît les besoins parce qu'il les a racontés pendant des années avec sa son micro et sa plume. Ali Bongo Leno, l'expertise du management culturel à portée Comme Hamza, Ali Bongo Leno est lui aussi un transfuge de la presse privée qui intègre nouvellement l'administration publique de la culture en Guinée. Nommé Directeur Général Adjoint des Industries Culturelles et Créatives, il arrive avec l’expertise du management culturel à portée de main. Connaisseur fin du milieu artistique, des acteurs culturels et des mécanismes de production et de diffusion, il incarne cette passerelle tant attendue entre la création et l'économie. Dans un secteur où le talent guinéen est immense mais encore sous-exploité, son rôle sera décisif: aider à structurer, professionnaliser et rendre viables les industries culturelles et créatives. Avec lui, la culture guinéenne ne sera plus seulement à célébrer, mais aussi à rentabiliser, au profit des artistes et du pays. Avec ces trois nominations parmi tant d’autres, c’est trois profils pour une même dynamique. Désormais, le Ministère dirigé par Moussa Moïse Sylla se renforce davantage et se dote sans aucun doute d'une équipe à la fois expérimentée, créative et enracinée dans le réel. La fougue, le professionnalisme et la connaissance du terrain sont désormais au service de la vision du Président Mamadi Doumbouya. Le chantier est immense, mais l'équipe est bien en place pour faire le job. Bernard Leno L’article Nominations au ministère de la Culture : trois hommes, la dynamique se poursuit et l’équipe se renforce est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: AFCON row: Morocco alleges Senegal FA chief contacted CAS arbitrator
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Morocco’s football federation has reported an alleged phone call between Senegal’s football chief and a Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) arbitrator, as the two countries await a ruling today on the disputed Africa Cup of Nations final. According to Reuters, a source with direct knowledge of the case said Morocco alleged that Senegalese Football Federation president Abdoulaye Fall spoke by phone with one of the three arbitrators on Sunday. Reuters said it could not independently verify whether the call took place or what was discussed. CAS is expected to issue its ruling on Senegal’s appeal on Tuesday afternoon. The appeal challenges the Confederation of African Football’s decision to overturn Senegal’s 1-0 extra-time victory in January’s final in Rabat and award Morocco a 3-0 win. CAF’s Appeal Board made its decision on March 17, ruling that Senegal had forfeited the match after its players temporarily left the pitch in protest at a late penalty awarded to Morocco. The players returned after a disruption of about 14 minutes, and Senegal went on to win the match. The African football governing body upheld Morocco’s position that Senegal’s departure breached Articles 82 and 84 of the competition regulations, which provide for a forfeiture and a 3-0 defeat. Senegal argues that because the match resumed and was completed, its victory should stand. CAS said on Monday that it had notified the Senegalese federation, CAF and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation that its ruling would be issued Tuesday afternoon. The court did not give an exact time. The post AFCON row: Morocco alleges Senegal FA chief contacted CAS arbitrator appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Helmet requirement for Pragyia was an error; the law will be corrected – NRSA boss
items.description: The Director-General of the National Road Safety Authority (NRSA), Abraham Amaliba, says the regulation requiring commercial tricycle operators, popularly known as pragyia riders, to wear helmets was included in error and will be repealed. He insists that the provision was not the intention of the framers of the law, arguing that the helmet requirement was meant for operators of aboboya tricycles used mainly for transporting goods, rather than commercial passenger tricycles. Speaking on Joy FM’s Midday News on Tuesday, November 24, Mr Amaliba argued that pragyia tricycles should be treated like mini-cars and, therefore, their drivers should not be required to wear helmets or provide them for passengers. “The provision that talks about tricycle drivers wearing a helmet is a mistake. That was not the intention of the framers of the law. Those who are supposed to wear helmets are the aboboya, and not tricycles,” he said. He drew a comparison between pragyia operators and taxi drivers, arguing that both vehicles serve similar passenger transport purposes and should be subject to comparable safety requirements. “A taxi is a minicar, and minicar drivers, or drivers who drive taxis, don’t wear helmets. So pragyia drivers are not supposed to wear helmets, and they are not even supposed to provide helmets for their passengers. So it’s a mistake,” he explained. Mr Amaliba said the confusion arose because both aboboya and pragyia vehicles are classified as tricycles under the regulations, despite serving different purposes. According to him, the authority intended the provision to cover aboboya operators, who use the vehicles mainly to transport goods and are required to wear helmets. He said the distinction was overlooked during the drafting of the regulation, resulting in the inclusion of commercial passenger tricycles in the helmet requirement. NRSA, MTTD to resolve enforcement concerns Addressing concerns about the continued enforcement of the regulation despite the NRSA’s position, Mr Amaliba said his office and the Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD) would need to meet to resolve the matter. He acknowledged the need for collaboration between the two institutions but maintained that the helmet requirement for pragyia operators was not intended. On when the provision would be repealed, the NRSA Director-General said he could not give a specific timeline. “I am not in a position to tell you, but there are people in Parliament who put up a bill, a regulation to deal with it,” he said. His comments come amid warnings by the MTTD that pragyia riders and passengers who fail to comply with the existing helmet requirements could face arrest, fines and imprisonment under Ghana’s road traffic regulations. Chief Inspector Frimpong Ayeh of the MTTD said the Oda Division was preparing to enforce the requirements, including the arrest of passengers found travelling without helmets.

items.title: 'Carrying hopes of 250m people': Zeeshan Ali to be 'first' Pakistani astronaut in space aboard China’s Shenzhou-24
items.description: Zeeshan Ali was named a crew member of China’s Shenzhou-24 space mission on Tuesday, which is scheduled to launch on November 25, with Ali set to become the first Pakistani to undertake an orbital space mission. Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, who is in China, referred to Ali on X as “Pakistan’s first astronaut”. Ali will also be the first foreign national to board Beijing’s Tiangong space station, the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) announced. “Pakistani astronaut Mohammad Zeeshan Ali is the first foreign national to visit Tiangong,” CMSA Spokesperson Zhang Jingbo said during a press conference. And the Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said the Pakistani astronaut was also the first international crew member to join China’s manned space programme. Jingbo said that the Long March-2F rocket that will carry the crew into space will soon be filled with propellant. “The crew is in good condition and the space station is functioning normally, meeting all requirements for the mission,” said Zhang. According to the CMSA, the Pakistani astronaut will serve as a payload specialist during the mission and return aboard the Shenzhou-23 spacecraft, which docked with the Tiangong space station in May. China’s astronaut Tang Hongbo will command the mission, with Wu Yi serving as the mission pilot and Ali taking on the role of payload specialist, according to the CMSA. The crewed spaceship is scheduled to be launched at 8:18am (Beijing Time and 5:18am Pakistan Time) on Wednesday from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China. Ali is expected to spend around a week in space, conducting various experiments alongside the Chinese crew. CMSA said that during the mission, the crew will conduct around 90 experiments. The Chinese space agency said the mission’s objectives included conducting an orbital rotation with the crew of the earlier Shenzhou-23 mission, carrying out routine operations and maintenance of the Chinese space station, and continuing space science research, including experiments involving space payloads. The crew currently aboard the Tiangong space station is headed by 40-year-old Zhu Yangzhu, Lai Ka-ying and Zhang Zhiyuan, also 40. Lai is Hong Kong’s first astronaut and the only woman currently aboard the space station. After the new crew reaches the space station, Ali will return to Earth alongside Lai and Zhang. Zhu will remain on board to complete China’s first full-year stay in space — a key test of endurance critical for future lunar and potentially deep-space ambitions. Zhu will be accompanied for the next six-month Tiangong rotation by 51-year-old space veteran Hongbo and Yi, in his late thirties and making his first voyage to space. ‘We have already made history’ Speaking at a press briefing in Jiayuguan, Ali said he was “deeply grateful” to the Chinese government for helping “us realise our dream of going into space”. He said he arrived at the Astronaut Centre of China a few months ago, carrying with him the hopes of 250 million Pakistani people. Detailing his experience in China, he said what he gained had far exceeded his initial expectations. “First, I have acquired space flight skills. The management, staff and instructors at the Astronaut Centre of China have provided me with comprehensive training […] Day after day, I take another step upward.” Pakistani astronaut Mohammad Zeeshan Ali. — Screengrab Moreover, he continued, “I have learned the Chinese language and developed a friendship with my Chinese colleagues. Now, I can communicate with my Chinese crewmates in Chinese.” “We trained side by side, and our friendship embodies the friendship between China and Pakistan: higher than the mountains, deeper than the oceans, sweeter than honey and as vast as outer space.” He said he had come to deeply appreciate the meaning of Chinese President Xi Jinping’s words: “Exploring the vast universe, developing the space industry and building China into a space power is our unremitting pursuit of the space dream.” “Now, this dream belongs to me and also belongs to Pakistan,” he said, adding that it would become a reality through the Shenzhou-24 space mission. He said he believed that “what comes after this flight matters more than the flight itself”. “This mission is not a finish line; it is a launch pad. And I hope the next chapter of China-Pakistan space cooperation will grow from one astronaut, one flight to multiple joint flights, to the Moon, Mars and beyond.” Ali noted that 2026 marked the 75th anniversary of China-Pakistan space cooperation, as well as the 75th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries. “Together with my Chinese crewmates, I will show that this friendship is real — not only on paper, but also in orbit.” Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo, Wu Yi and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali gesture as they attend a press conference before the Shenzhou-24 spaceflight mission to China’s Tiangong space station, at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, near Jiuquan, Gansu province, China on November 24, 2026. —Reuters Addressing Pakistanis, he said: “I now feel the true weight of the words of our Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, when he told me that we were about to write a new chapter in Pakistan’s history. I want to assure you that I am not flying for myself. I carry the name of Pakistan on my shoulder, the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis. “To every child who is watching while I am in orbit, just look up at the sky and remember that I am up there with your dreams.” In his message to his family, he said: “I want to say that I will travel farther from home than ever before. But I promise you one thing: whenever I look back at the Earth for the first time, I will always search for the light of our home before I look at anything else. No matter how far I fly, we will still share the same Moon, and I will still be looking back at the same Earth.” He then thanked his teammates, those who supported him, his instructors, scientists, engineers, Pakistan’s space agency Suparco and CMSA. “You are the reason that I am here today, and no matter who flies, we have already made history together,” he said. Ali said the “two great nations of China and Pakistan have turned a pilot into an astronaut in a remarkably short span of time. Now it is time to show this great achievement, innovation and send the world a message that we work hand in hand for the peaceful utilisation of space”. Separately, China Daily posted a video of Ali saying that his planned one-year training had been compressed to seven months. “That was the biggest challenge for me when I came here. But the real challenge, honestly speaking, was mastering the Chinese language. Learning the Chinese language is the key to the hearts of Chinese people,” he added. Ali said he had read about several astronauts saying that whenever they looked at Earth from outer space, they did not see any borders or “separation between human beings; it is one humanity”. He said he would be taking handwritten letters from his children and father on his journey “as a great source of inspiration”. ‘A moment that belongs to every Pakistani’ Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif took to X to wish the crew his best for Wednesday’s liftoff. “Tomorrow, Pakistan will look to the skies with anticipation, pride and deep gratitude,” he said, adding that as the Shenzhou-24 prepared to carry a Pakistani astronaut to Tiangong Space Station, the nation stood on the “threshold of a historic first”. “It is a moment that belongs to every Pakistani,” he wrote and paid tribute to Suparco as well as academic institutions, scientists, the armed forces and national institutions whose efforts reflected “Pakistan’s growing capabilities and our determination to reach new frontiers in space exploration and scientific advancement”. PM Shehbaz expressed gratitude to President Xi, stating that his “visionary” leadership had taken Pakistan-China friendship to an “unprecedented height”. “This historic milestone is a powerful testament to the exceptional trust, mutual respect and enduring brotherhood that bind our two nations and peoples,” Shehbaz wrote, as he wished the crew his best for a safe and successful mission. “Pakistan-China friendship is surpassing the heights of the Himalayas, in its journey to outer space.” President Asif Ali Zardari also congratulated the nation on “historic” participation in the Chinese mission, calling it a “landmark achievement” and a “moment of immense national pride”, according to a statement issued by his office. He said the mission reflected Pakistan’s “growing commitment to science, research and technological advancement”, lauding the role of Suparco, Pakistani scientists and China’s cooperation. President Zardari expressed hope that the mission would open new horizons for Pakistan’s space programme and the scientific experiments undertaken during the mission would contribute to advancing research and knowledge. “Pakistan’s participation in human spaceflight is not only about reaching space but also about harnessing its opportunities for research, learning and innovation. Citing a verse from national poet Allama Iqbal — Sitaron se aagay jahan aur bhi hain — he stressed that the mission should inspire Pakistan’s young generation to “pursue knowledge, innovation and scientific discovery with confidence and ambition”. Planning Minister Iqbal also congratulated Ali and said the joint mission marked “the trust and iron brotherhood between Pakistan and China”. Sharing a photo of himself from the press briefing in Jiayuguan, Ahsan posted on X: “Filled with immense pride and excitement as I witness history in the making. “Watching our astronaut, Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, take centre stage is a deeply moving moment. We had dared to dream big and laid the foundational blocks for Pakistan’s space and science ambitions. Today, seeing those dreams take flight and come true right before our eyes reaffirms that no frontier is beyond our reach when a nation commits to knowledge, innovation, and perseverance. The sky is no longer our limit—it is our launching pad.” Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar congratulated the entire nation and Suparco as “Pakistan prepares to make history in space exploration and joint scientific advancement”. “​With China’s Shenzhou-24 mission set for launch, a Pakistani astronaut, Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, will soon enter orbit as the first international crew member aboard the Tiangong space station. This landmark moment speaks volumes about the strength of our all-weather strategic cooperative partnership. “​My sincere wishes go out to all the astronauts on board for a smooth and successful mission. Long live Pakistan-China friendship!” he posted on X. Information Minister Attaullah Tarar posted on X that a Pakistani astronaut going into space was a source of joy and pride for the entire nation. Earlier in April, astronauts Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud were chosen from Pakistan to start training in China. Suparco and CMSA signed a cooperation agreement in February 2025, under which two Pakistanis were to train in China, with one joining a mission on the Tiangong space station operated by Beijing. Eventually, Ali was chosen to join the Chinese mission. Making the announcement, Iqbal wrote on X that he wanted to “honour both of our astronauts, Muhammad Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud, selected for final training. They were chosen from among Pakistan’s finest pilots and scientists. They trained in centrifuges and simulators, in emergency drills and in a new language. Both performed exceptionally well in training. Though Zeeshan Ali will fly tomorrow, both have already made Pakistan proud”. PM Shehbaz had met the two in April and congratulated them on their selection. He said the space mission was a “matter of pride for the entire nation” and further commended their “round-the-clock efforts” in achieving the milestone. PM Shehbaz had hoped that the space mission would “add new dimensions to the brotherly relationship between Pakistan and China”. Beijing has invested heavily in its space programme in recent years — catching up with its main rival the United States — and aims to land astronauts on the Moon by 2030. Pakistan is a natural partner, given the country’s decades-long, “all-weather” friendship. China is Pakistan’s largest trading partner and a major foreign investor. China has been barred from participating in the International Space Station since 2011, when the US prohibited Nasa from collaborating with Chinese space agencies. Since then, Beijing has sought to build partnerships with other countries — including Pakistan — in its expanding space programme.

items.title: Reacting to Bilawal's remarks on 'brute majority', a section of legal community wants 26th, 27th Amendments repealed
items.description: A hundred members of the legal fraternity and civil society have called for the 26th and 27th Constitutional Amendments to be repealed, reacting to remarks by PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, whose party had made their enactment possible. The 26th and 27th Amendments, enacted in October 2024 and November 2025 respectively, were passed by both houses of the Parliament amid outcry from the PTI-led opposition. Last week, Bilawal — a strong advocate for both Amendments when they were passed — said the 27th Amendment was “passed neither through political consensus nor mutual agreement; it was passed with brute majority”, and that the previous one did have mutual agreement. He also questioned the current status of the judiciary, particularly in the wake of the 27th Amendment, noting that resignations of senior judges followed the legislation. Later, the PPP chairman clarified that he was “not disowning” the 27th Amendment, but rather noting that it did not enjoy the same “unanimous consensus” as the 18th Amendment and the 1973 Constitution. In an open letter on Tuesday, 100 individuals — mostly lawyers and also including activists and academics — called for both the 26th and 27th Amendments to be repealed. “Pakistan’s constitutional order belongs to its people. It cannot be seized by a majority that its own members admit was never theirs to wield,” read the letter, also signed by retired Supreme Court Justice Mansoor Ali Shah. The letter recalled that Bilawal “admitted that the 27th Amendment was passed neither through political consensus nor through agreement, but a ‘brute majority’”. It demanded that the “constitutional order that existed prior to the 26th Amendment must be restored”, adding that any future reform of the judiciary must come through an “open and consultative process”. The 26th Amendment carved a constitutional bench out of the SC, with its members chosen by a reconstituted Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) in which judges no longer held a majority. A year later, the 27th Amendment turned those benches into an entirely separate court, the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC), which is said to have effectively dethroned the SC as the country’s highest judicial forum. It also made significant changes to the judicial system and the military’s chain of command , and granted immunities to government officials. Two of the SC’s senior-most judges, including Shah, resigned in protest the day it became law. Tuesday’s letter also called for reserved seats in the legislative houses to be returned to their “lawful claimants”, in an apparent reference to the opposition. The PTI was deprived of its reserved seats in the 2024 elections following the revocation of its electoral symbol. Although an SC bench declared the PTI eligible for the seats, the order was not implemented and later overturned by the constitutional bench created via the 26th Amendment, which handed them to the coalition parties that challenged the 2024 ruling. “The government cannot continue exercising parliamentary authority derived from a process that the governing coalition’s own leadership has now publicly called into question,” Tuesday’s letter read. “These seats must be restored to their rightful claimants through the appropriate legal and constitutional mechanism,” it added. The letter noted that Bilawal “described the way the opposition was stripped of its reserved seats as ‘a joke’ and said the treasury benches had simply put those seats ‘in their pockets’”. “Most damning of all, he accused the ruling government of amending the Constitution using seats that are ‘not yours’,” the document added. The signatories pointed out that these words came “from the government’s key coalition partner whose votes were required to pass both the 26th and 27th Amendments”. It continued: “The treasury benches face a question they can no longer evade. Their own coalition partner says reserved seats were taken by parties that had no right to them. “On what constitutional, legal or moral basis does the government then keep claiming the numbers through which the 26th and 27th Amendments were passed?” The lawyers and activists noted that a two-thirds majority was the safeguard the Constitution demands so that “it cannot be changed without the genuine and lawful representation of the people’s will”. However, a majority “made up with seats that were unjustly denied to the opposition is not the majority the Constitution demands”, they contended. “An amendment passed on that basis holds no constitutional, legal, or democratic validity. An amendment passed without a legitimate two-thirds majority is void from its very inception,” the letter asserted. It further said that these questions applied directly to the FCC, which “owes its existence wholly to the 27th Amendment”. “Its jurisdiction, its composition and its authority all come from a constitutional change whose legitimacy is now openly repudiated by the very people who brought it into being. “A court cannot rise higher than its source. An institution whose authors cannot defend how it was built has no foundation left to stand on,” the lawyer said. “Pakistan has witnessed far too many admissions of wrongdoing that have led to no consequences,” the letter observed, noting that leaders acknowledge violations at press conferences, express reservations, and then “allow the very arrangements they condemn to continue unchanged”. “This cycle must end. The question is no longer simply whether a wrong was committed, but whether consequences and meaningful action will follow.” The signatories stressed this was a “moment to begin repairing the grave damage caused to the judiciary and the constitutional order”. “Those in power have a choice. They can either continue to cling to an illegitimate majority or they can correct course.”

items.title: Pakistani Prisoners Face Poor Access to Health Care
items.description: Click to expand Image People exit the main entrance of the Karachi Central Prison in Karachi, Pakistan, January 28, 2021. © 2021 AP Photo/Fareed Khan When Pakistani senators visited the prototype Islamabad Model Jail on November 19 and inspected the healthcare facilities that would be available to prisoners, they called them “adequate.” But the conditions they observed on their curated tour are a far cry from the reality most prisoners experience in Pakistan’s justice system. Human Rights Watch has documented structural and systemic problems in Pakistan’s jails and prisons that leave most inmates with little access to health care. Many inmates who fall ill in custody fail to receive prompt or decent care at all. After two prisoners died in Peshawar Central Prison following alleged delays in medical treatment, a lawyer petitioned the Peshawar High Court asking that prisons across the province be required to record when prisoners request medical help and establish clear procedures for emergency hospital transfers. Colonial-era laws have long-enabled Pakistani officials and powerful people to interfere in prison operations, sometimes making use of poor conditions to harass jailed political opponents. In a November 16 letter released by his lawyer, former Prime Minister Imran Khan appealed for urgent medical care for himself and his wife, Bushra Bibi, citing his high blood pressure and her need for eye surgery. Khan’s appeal echoes complaints about medical care in custody from former President Asif Ali Zardari and former Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif. All have alleged that prison services denied access to medical care as a form of punishment. Federal and provincial governments in Pakistan should bring health care in jails and prisons in line with international standards, notably the United Nations Standard Minimum Rules for the Treatment of Prisoners (the Mandela Rules), which require that prisoners receive necessary free medical care to the same standard available in the community, with prompt attention in emergencies. In October, Justice Project Pakistan called for common standards across provinces so prisoners can see medical specialists when needed and continue treatment after release. Pakistan’s federal and provincial governments should provide prescribed medicines free of charge and require prisons to record how long patients wait for care. When care requires an urgent hospital transfer, prison authorities should promptly facilitate transport. Authorities should ensure all prisoners, regardless of political affiliation or status, receive timely and adequate medical care, with continuity of treatment.

items.description: La Banque centrale europeenne (BCE) tire a son tour la sonnette d'alarme sur les dangers lies a l'hyperconcentration des investissements dans l'intelligence artificielle. Les besoins de capitaux des grandes entreprises technologiques americaines, notamment pour les centres de donnees, atteignent des niveaux historiques et s'appuient de plus en plus sur la dette. Deja, en janvier 2026, le Forum economique mondial evoquait cette menace dans son rapport annuel sur les « risques mondiaux » . Des investissements colossaux et une concentration inquietante Selon le rapport, les depenses d'investissements cumulees de ces societes devraient atteindre 5 500 milliards de dollars d'ici 2030. Apres avoir puise dans leurs reserves et leve des fonds, elles se tournent largement vers les marches obligataires. La concentration des emissions de dette est en passe de depasser le pic de la bulle Internet en pourcentage du PIB americain. « Historiquement, de telles tendances ont souvent coïncide avec des sommets du marche, signalant une exuberance de fin de cycle », soulignent les auteurs. Sur les reseaux sociaux, la question est suivie de pres. Un internaute nuance neanmoins « Cela ne signifie pas qu'une crise est inevitable ». 🤖 La BCE alerte sur les risques financiers liés à l'IA : valorisations ambitieuses, dette et financements circulaires. Cela ne signifie pas qu'une crise est inévitable. Un sujet à suivre avec nuance. #IA #Économie https://t.co/HeOufZiEEd — JyhelVibe (@JyhelVibe) November 23, 2026 Les valorisations actuelles reposent sur des previsions de benefices tres ambitieuses. Les capitalisations des geants de l'IA ont deja chute de plusieurs milliers de milliards de dollars ces dernieres semaines. La faible volatilite anticipee des marches pourrait indiquer qu'une correction brutale reste un « risque sous-estime ». L'Europe n'est pas epargnee, elle qui a investi massivement dans le secteur . Une part significative des emissions de dette liees a l'IA a ete realisee en euros, et les investisseurs de la zone euro ont accru leur exposition, notamment via les fonds et autres acteurs non bancaires, moins regules. Une baisse des valorisations pourrait se propager rapidement au systeme financier et a l'economie reelle. Ces emissions en euros concurrent egalement les etats membres qui refinancent leur propre dette, les obligeant a offrir des taux plus eleves alors que certains affichent deja des deficits persistants. items.title: Nissan Africa delegation commends Japan Motors’ investment in modern service facilities
items.description: A high-level delegation from Nissan Motor Corporation, led by its Managing Director for Africa, Mohammed Abdel Samad, visited Japan Motors Trading Company Ltd. (JMTC), toured the company’s operations, and expressed admiration for its newly refurbished, ultramodern service centre. The visit gave the Nissan delegation deeper insight into Japan Motors’ operations, its contribution to Nissan’s business in Ghana, and its investments in strengthening customer experience and after-sales service delivery. During the visit, the delegation toured the Nissan vehicle assembly plant, inspected the company’s showrooms and service facilities, interacted with customers, and engaged with local management and operational teams on market developments, customer expectations and opportunities for growth. A major highlight of the visit was the newly refurbished Japan Motors service centre, a significant investment that enhances the company’s after-sales operations and provides customers with a more convenient, comfortable, and efficient service experience. The modern facility has been redesigned to improve the entire customer service process, from vehicle reception and complaint registration to job-card processing and vehicle servicing. It features improved reception processes, modern service facilities, and enhanced digital solutions to deliver a seamless customer experience. As part of its digital transformation drive, Japan Motors has also enhanced its online customer services through its website, www.nissanghana.com, allowing customers to conveniently book vehicle servicing appointments, purchase genuine Nissan spare parts and reserve their preferred Nissan vehicles online. These digital solutions give customers greater access and convenience while improving service coordination and operational efficiency. Notable improvements at the service centre include a more spacious, luxurious customer waiting area furnished with comfortable sofas; digital display screens showcasing Japan Motors’ products and services; and a barcode-enabled system that gives customers easy access to its online services. These enhancements are expected to improve customer convenience, streamline service reception procedures, reduce waiting times and strengthen the overall efficiency of the company’s after-sales operations. Speaking about the investment, Mr Amine Kabbara, Managing Director of Japan Motors Ghana, said the refurbishment forms part of the company’s commitment to continuously improving customer satisfaction and raising the standard of its after-sales services. He described the Nissan delegation’s visit as a reaffirmation of the longstanding partnership between Nissan Motor Corporation and Japan Motors, particularly in strengthening the brand’s presence and identifying new opportunities within Ghana and the wider West African automotive market. Mr. Amine Kabbara expressed appreciation to the Nissan delegation for the visit, noting that Japan Motors values its partnership with Nissan and looks forward to working together to further strengthen the brand’s presence across West Africa. Mr Abdel Samad noted the value of engaging directly with local partners, customers and operational teams, emphasising the importance of strong partnerships, operational excellence and a customer-focused approach in supporting Nissan’s growth ambitions across Africa. He applauded Japan Motors for its continued investments in vehicle assembly, sales, after-sales services, and digital customer solutions, describing these initiatives as important steps toward improving customer satisfaction and further promoting the Nissan brand in Ghana.

items.title: 2027: Zamfara people firmly behind APC despite insults, criticism — Yari
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Director-General of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul’azeez Yari Abubakar, says the people of Zamfara are firmly behind the party despite criticism and what he called insults directed at it. Yari spoke on Monday at the APC governorship campaign flag-off in Talata-Mafara, Zamfara State. He said the turnout showed the party had the support it needed to win elections at every level in 2027. “Make sure this message gets to the public: we are determined to deliver victory for the APC, from President Tinubu down to members of the State House of Assembly,” Yari said. “The overwhelming response to our call demonstrates that, despite the insults and campaigns against the APC, the people of Zamfara have understood our message and are firmly behind the party.” Supporters gathered at the town’s Eid ground for the rally after welcoming Governor Dauda Lawal’s motorcade to Talata-Mafara, according to the report. Lawal thanked the crowd and praised supporters for their solidarity, resilience and commitment to peaceful coexistence. “Whenever I turn around and see this mammoth crowd of supporters, I am filled with gratitude,” he said, adding, “At this point, I will simply say, Let us wait for election day and, ultimately, the swearing-in day.” The APC campaign train is expected to visit other local government areas in Zamfara as the party continues its mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections. items.title: Mahama urges German firms to use Ghana as gateway to Africa’s $3.5tn market
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has urged German companies to consider Ghana as a strategic entry point into the African market, which he says offers significant investment and production opportunities under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). In his Presidential Opening Address at the 6th German-African Business Summit in Accra on Tuesday, November 24, he said Africa should be viewed as an interconnected market rather than a collection of isolated economies. “I therefore wish to invite German companies to consider Africa not as a collection of isolated markets, but as a crystallising network of interconnected investment and production opportunities, and to consider Ghana as one of your strategic entry points into that market,” he said. The President said the AfCFTA provides access to a continental market of approximately 1.4 billion people, with a combined gross domestic product estimated at more than $3.5 trillion. He said the agreement presents opportunities for businesses to expand trade, strengthen investment cooperation and develop production networks across the continent. Mr Mahama also urged African leaders to improve border administration, transport infrastructure, customs procedures, payment systems and regulatory coordination to maximise the benefits of continental integration. He said Ghana was positioning itself as a competitive destination for investment, manufacturing, innovation and regional trade, while encouraging partnerships that would create jobs, strengthen local enterprises and promote economic growth.

items.title: AFCON Controversy: Hakimi speaks ahead of CAS verdict
items.description: Morocco captain Achraf Hakimi has criticised Senegal’s decision to walk off the pitch during the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations final, insisting that teams should not abandon a match in such circumstances. Hakimi made the remarks on Tuesday during a press conference ahead of Paris Saint-Germain’s Champions League clash against AS Roma, as the Court of Arbitration for Sport prepares to deliver its judgment on Senegal’s appeal against the decision to award Morocco the AFCON title later today, Tuesday 24th November. “We wait for the verdict but in my view, you can’t leave the pitch in that way as Senegal did,” the PSG defender said. He, however, expressed pride in Morocco’s performance and said he would wait for the outcome of the proceedings. “I am proud of my team; and we will see what happens. “For me will be a calm day. Train, go home, then someone will tell me the verdict and I will go to sleep ahead of tomorrow game”, he added. Recall Vanguard reported that Senegal appealed to CAS after the Confederation of African Football’s Appeal Board overturned the result of the January 18 final and awarded Morocco a 3-0 victory. Senegal had originally defeated hosts Morocco 1-0 after extra time in Rabat, with Pape Gueye scoring the winning goal. However, the final was thrown into controversy after Senegalese players walked off the pitch for about 14 minutes in protest against a late penalty awarded to Morocco. Morocco’s Brahim Diaz failed to convert the spot kick after play resumed, while Senegal went on to score in extra time and claim the trophy. In March, CAF’s Appeal Board ruled that Senegal had forfeited the match by leaving the pitch without authorisation, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory and the continental title. Senegal subsequently challenged the decision at CAS, arguing that the referee had allowed the match to resume and that the original result should stand. The case was heard at CAS headquarters in Lausanne, Switzerland, on October 8, with the court expected to announce its decision on Tuesday. Meanwhile, PSG are scheduled to face Roma at the Parc des Princes on Wednesday in a Matchday Five fixture of the UEFA Champions League. The post AFCON Controversy: Hakimi speaks ahead of CAS verdict appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: CSOs demand transparency over ECG private-sector reforms
items.description: Civil society organisations monitoring Ghana’s energy sector are demanding greater transparency in the planned private-sector reforms of the Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG), insisting that prospective investors must demonstrate clear Ghanaian ownership and investment commitments. The Ghana CSOs Alliance on Mission 300 wants the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Energy and Green Transition to disclose the ownership structures and funding sources of companies seeking to participate in electricity distribution before any agreements are signed. The groups argue that such disclosures would enable the public to establish who is financing the proposed transactions, who stands to benefit and whether the arrangements would serve Ghana’s economic interests. Speaking on behalf of the alliance, its Convenor and Executive Coordinator of the Strategic Youth Network for Development, Chibeze Ezekiel, said private-sector participation must create opportunities for Ghanaian businesses rather than facilitate foreign takeovers with limited benefits for local communities. He welcomed the government’s commitment to achieving full private-sector participation in electricity distribution by the end of 2027, supported by binding targets to reduce distribution losses and improve revenue collection. However, he stressed that the initiative would only meet the expectations of civil society groups if ownership and investment capital remained substantially Ghanaian. “The commitment to full private-sector participation in distribution by end-2027, with binding loss and collection targets, answers directly to what we have been demanding so long as ownership and capital remain substantially Ghanaian,” he said. Mr Ezekiel said the government must ensure that the involvement of private companies translates into stronger domestic investment and greater participation by Ghanaian-owned businesses. “We call on the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Energy and Green Transition to ensure that bringing private companies into electricity distribution means Ghanaian companies building local ownership and local money, not foreign takeovers that don’t benefit citizens,” he stated. CSOs seek stronger local participation Beyond the question of ownership, the alliance wants the proposed restructuring to strengthen the capacity of Ghanaian businesses to participate meaningfully in electricity distribution. It argues that attracting private investors should not be the sole measure of success, particularly if local companies are left without significant opportunities to invest, develop expertise or contribute to the management of the distribution system. The groups are therefore advocating a framework that combines private-sector investment with domestic capital mobilisation, local business development and improved accountability. They also believe that greater transparency in prospective transactions would help ensure that the selection of private-sector partners reflects the country’s long-term economic interests. August dialogue informs demands The alliance’s position follows an energy-sector dialogue held in August 2026, which identified ECG reform and the monitoring of specific commitments under the 2026 Energy Compact as priority areas. The discussions highlighted the need to address operational challenges in electricity distribution, particularly losses and weaknesses in revenue collection. The CSOs want the planned reforms to deliver measurable improvements in these areas while creating opportunities for Ghanaian businesses to develop the expertise and capacity needed to contribute to the sector. They maintain that the success of private-sector participation should be measured not only by the investment it attracts but also by its impact on operational efficiency, local ownership and the wider economy. The alliance is consequently urging the two ministries to ensure that the reform process is transparent and accountable, with Ghanaian businesses positioned to play a substantial role in the future of electricity distribution.

items.title: Christian men’s groups urge emotional openness, gender respect, and youth mentorship on International Men’s Day
items.description: Christian men’s groups in Ghana have called for a shift in traditional expectations surrounding masculinity, urging men to share responsibilities with women, seek help when overwhelmed, and actively mentor younger generations. The call was made at the National Christian Men’s Forum in Accra, which brought together its members to mark International Men’s Day. Speakers at the forum noted that societal pressure on men to appear stoic, bear financial and emotional burdens alone, and keep personal struggles to themselves is harming families and preventing many from accessing needed support. Raising Responsible Boys A major focus of the discussions was how young boys are raised and the attitudes they form toward women and girls. Speaking at the event, a member of the Wesleyan Men’s Board and the African Methodist Council Men’s Movement, Dr. George Prah, stressed that tackling gender-based violence requires intentional mentorship from an early age. “We can also mentor our boys as a long-term measure to end the menace. We must raise boys who respect girls. We must raise boys who understand consent. We must raise boys who know that crying is not weakness. And we must raise boys who know that violence is not manhood,” Dr. Prah said. He added that responsible men must see women as equal partners in their homes, churches, and communities. Breaking the Stigma Around Vulnerability Kojo Sackey, a member of the Public Affairs Directorate of the Full Gospel Businessmen’s Fellowship International, encouraged men to embrace vulnerability and manage life’s pressures responsibly rather than carrying excessive burdens alone. “As men, we should be ready to take up the responsibility and fulfill our mandate on earth, and as men, it is okay to need help, it is okay to cry if it becomes necessary. We are not supposed to carry too much burden, but to manage it as and when it becomes necessary,” Mr. Sackey stated. Bridging the Generational Divide Beyond mental well-being and gender relations, speakers highlighted the growing disconnect between older and younger generations. Mr. Sackey urged older men to take an active interest in guiding Gen Zs and Millennials through mentorship rather than criticizing their choices, while encouraging young people to remain receptive to counsel. “To the younger generation, we want to tell them that there is no difficult generation on this earth. We know we have the Gen Zs, we have the Millennials, we have the Gen Xs… The older generation is ready to offload wisdom. We should be ready as Gen Zs and Millennials also to accept them with understanding,” he added.

items.title: ‘Africa and Europe need each other’ – German President
items.description: German President Dr Frank-Walter Steinmeier has called for stronger cooperation between Africa and Europe, saying the two continents need each other to address shared global challenges and secure economic prosperity. Delivering an address at the opening of the 6th German-African Business Summit in Accra on Tuesday, November 24, he said climate change, hunger, poverty and the rapid development of artificial intelligence required joint solutions. “At all times, I was guided by the firm conviction that Africa and Europe need each other. In today’s world, that sentence contains the new urgency,” he said. Dr Steinmeier said climate change was having a particularly severe impact on African countries, while other global challenges could not be addressed effectively by individual countries acting alone. He also praised the creativity, courage and entrepreneurial spirit of young Africans, saying their energy offered significant opportunities for cooperation and innovation. The German President said stronger economic ties would help create jobs, generate prosperity and open up opportunities for businesses on both continents. He urged German companies to explore investment opportunities in Africa, adding: “Be curious, take risks, and invest in our common future.”

items.title: Pragyia riders, passengers risk up to 8 months in jail for riding without helmets
items.description: Commercial tricycle operators, popularly known as pragyia riders, and their passengers risk prosecution, fines and possible imprisonment for failing to comply with road safety requirements on protective helmets and reflective clothing. Under Ghana’s road traffic regulations, both riders and passengers are required to wear appropriate protective helmets with securely fastened chin straps, as well as reflective clothing. Speaking on the enforcement of the regulations, Chief Inspector Frimpong Ayeh of the Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD) said the requirements apply to both operators and passengers, contrary to the perception that tricycles offer the same level of protection as cars. “The Oda Division has warned that as part of its upcoming enforcement operations, passengers found travelling without helmets will also be arrested,” he cautioned. A legal explanation of the provisions indicates that Regulation 109 of the Road Traffic Regulations, 2012 (L.I. 2180), requires riders and passengers to wear reflective clothing and appropriate helmets that fit properly, with their chin straps securely fastened. The regulation also places responsibility on riders to ensure that passengers below the age of 18 comply with the safety requirements. Offenders convicted under the provision face a fine of between 25 and 50 penalty units, imprisonment for between one and three months, or both. However, Regulation 176(2) provides an additional penalty for commercial passengers who travel without protective helmets. Offenders are liable to a fine of between 25 and 50 penalty units, imprisonment for up to eight months, or both. Difference between pragyia and Okada regulations A distinction exists between the regulations governing commercial motorcycle operators, popularly known as Okada riders, and those covering pragyia operators. While the regulations expressly require Okada riders to provide their passengers with protective crash helmets that meet approved standards, there is no equivalent explicit requirement for pragyia operators. The regulations governing Okada operations also require riders to ensure that passengers’ helmets are securely fastened and maintained in a clean, dry and wearable condition. The differences in the provisions highlight the need for clarity on the specific safety obligations of commercial tricycle operators and their passengers as enforcement of road safety regulations intensifies.
