items.description: Le club égyptien d'Al Ahly a annoncé, mardi, le limogeage de son entraîneur marocain Houcine Ammouta. Dans un communiqué publié sur son site officiel, Al Ahly a indiqué avoir remercié Houcine Ammouta et son staff technique pour la période durant laquelle ils ont assuré la direction de l'équipe première de football. Nommé à la tête du club égyptien le 15 juin dernier, Houcine Ammouta a dirigé l'équipe lors de 14 rencontres toutes compétitions confondues (championnat égyptien, Coupe de la CAF, Coupe d'Égypte et Coupe de la Ligue), enregistrant un bilan de 11 victoires, deux matchs nuls et une seule défaite. Sous la houlette du technicien marocain, Al Ahly a inscrit 30 buts, soit une moyenne de plus de deux réalisations par match, contre seulement neuf buts encaissés en 14 rencontres. L'unique défaite d'Ammouta à la tête d'Al Ahly remonte à lundi soir, lorsque son équipe s'est inclinée face à Pyramids FC (0-2), lors du choc de la 9e journée du championnat égyptien de première division. À la faveur de cette victoire, Pyramids FC a conforté sa place de leader avec 27 points, tandis qu'Al Ahly a rétrogradé à la troisième position avec 20 points. En moins de deux ans, le club égyptien a limogé quatre entraîneurs, à savoir le Suisse Marcel Koller, l'Espagnol José Riveiro, le Danois Jess Thorup et le Marocain Houcine Ammouta. The post Al Ahly d'Égypte se sépare de son entraîneur marocain Houcine Ammouta appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: German President urges faster implementation of African Continental Free Trade Area
items.description: German President Dr Frank-Walter Steinmeier has urged African countries to accelerate the implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), describing the agreement as a crucial step towards expanding trade and economic growth on the continent. “The African Union’s African Continental Free Trade Area, the largest of its kind in the world, is indeed a crucial step here. And it gives me reason for optimism,” he said in his Presidential Opening Address at the 6th German-African Business Summit in Accra on Tuesday, November 24. He said the agreement offered significant opportunities to strengthen intra-African trade and deepen economic cooperation with Germany. Dr Steinmeier called on African countries not to abandon the reforms needed to facilitate trade and open new trade routes across the continent. “Please do not waver in your endeavours to implement necessary reforms and create ways to facilitate trade on your continent and open up new trade routes,” he said. He said the measures were essential to driving growth and prosperity and expanding mutually beneficial cooperation. “Both things are essential for greater growth and prosperity, as well as for the expansion of our cooperation in our mutual interests,” he added. The German President said economic growth must also create opportunities for young people, giving them better prospects for the future. “The key to this is economic growth, economic growth that gives young people prospects for a better life,” he said.

items.title: German President backs Africa’s call for stronger representation at UN
items.description: German President Dr Frank-Walter Steinmeier has backed calls for Africa to have a stronger voice in the United Nations, saying the continent deserves greater representation in shaping the global order. He said the global rules-based order was facing growing threats, with wars and conflicts disrupting international trade, the movement of goods and raw materials, and livelihoods, particularly in Africa. Dr Steinmeier said the challenges facing the international community required stronger cooperation and reliable partnerships rather than isolation. “What we need is more cooperation and reliability, not less,” he said in his Presidential Opening Address at the 6th German-African Business Summit in Accra on Tuesday, November 24. He said Germany supported efforts to make the international system fairer and more inclusive. He called for new partnerships built on fair rules, stressing that countries needed dependable allies to address shared economic and geopolitical challenges. The German President also urged African countries to continue implementing reforms and facilitating trade to strengthen their economies and expand cooperation with Germany. He said Germany and its companies were ready to support the continent’s development. “I can assure you, Germany and German companies are reliable, strong, and transparent partners on this path, actors who keep their word,” he said. The 6th German-African Business Summit, which runs from November 23 to 25, 2026, is bringing together policymakers, business executives and investors to explore opportunities for stronger economic relations between Germany and African countries.

items.title: Some students engage in promiscuous and illegal acts to pay costly hostel fees – NUGS President
items.description: The President of the National Union of Ghana Students (NUGS), Rashid Ibrahim, has raised concerns about the financial difficulties confronting tertiary students, saying some are compelled to engage in promiscuous and illegal activities to raise money to pay for hostel fees. He attributed the situation to financial constraints within the tertiary education system, arguing that the lack of adequate accommodation support and the pressure of meeting academic and residential expenses have left some students struggling to remain in school. Speaking on PM Express on November 23, Mr Ibrahim said the problem extended beyond students who were unable to secure accommodation, with many facing deferment of their academic programmes because they could not meet the associated financial obligations. He disclosed that, in his capacity as NUGS President, he had personally received numerous requests from students seeking financial assistance to secure accommodation. According to him, he had supported some of them with his personal funds, while the number of students requiring such assistance continued to grow. “I can tell you that the people who have actually hit me in my DM, for me to support them with accommodation, are around 20 to 30 people,” he said. Mr Ibrahim said the situation was particularly worrying given the number of students across the country who had been forced to defer their programmes because of financial difficulties. He estimated that the number of students affected by deferment could run into thousands, describing the situation as a reflection of the broader challenges facing tertiary education. “Those who are deferred across the country, I can confidently say that they are in the thousands. And that is a fact,” he stated. Financial hardship pushes students into risky activities Beyond deferment and difficulties securing accommodation, the NUGS President said some students had resorted to activities he described as promiscuous and illegal in an attempt to raise money for their hostel fees. He said the financial pressure on students had created circumstances in which some felt compelled to find alternative means of meeting their educational expenses, even when those choices exposed them to risks. “And not only deferment. Some people actually engage in some promiscuous acts just to make sure that their hostel fees are being paid. And it is not their fault,” he said. Mr Ibrahim argued that the situation should not be viewed solely as a consequence of individual decisions, but rather as a symptom of a system that had failed to adequately address students’ financial and accommodation needs. He maintained that students facing such difficulties were often left with limited options, particularly when they had to meet accommodation costs alongside other academic expenses. “I don’t blame them, but it’s a system that has created all this,” he added. NUGS President calls for student-friendly education system Mr Ibrahim called for reforms that would guarantee students greater academic freedom and reduce the financial pressures that interfere with their ability to pursue their education. He argued that a fairer tertiary education system, with adequate support for students, would help address the circumstances pushing some into risky and unlawful activities to meet their financial obligations. “If you have a fair system that gives the students that academic freedom, I don’t think that the students will engage in some promiscuous act, some illegal acts to make sure that they pay their school fees,” he stated. His comments come amid continuing disagreement over accommodation charges at the University of Ghana. For the 2026/2027 academic year, the University of Ghana reduced a proposed 26 per cent increase in fees for standard four-bed rooms in its four Diaspora halls to 15 per cent following consultations with student leaders.

items.title: Court nullifies Omo-Agege’s NDC senatorial candidacy, orders INEC to delist him
items.description: The Federal High Court sitting in Warri, Delta State, on Tuesday nullified the nomination of former Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, as the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections, citing non-compliance with the provisions of the Electoral Act. The court, presided over by Justice Hyeladzira Ajiya Nganjiwa, ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to remove Omo-Agege’s name from its list of candidates for the election and restrained the former Deputy Senate President from parading himself as the NDC senatorial candidate. In a further setback for the NDC, the court held that the statutory window for conducting fresh primaries to nominate another candidate had elapsed, noting that the Electoral Act prescribed a timeline of 180 days before the general elections. The judgment followed a suit instituted by Prof. Alexander Osondu Akpodiete, marked FHC/WR/CS/120/2026, challenging the validity of Omo-Agege’s nomination on grounds bordering on his resignation from the All Progressives Congress (APC), membership of the NDC and eligibility to participate in the party’s senatorial primary. Omo-Agege’s objection Delivering judgment, Justice Nganjiwa dismissed all five preliminary objections raised by Omo-Agege, the NDC and INEC challenging the competence of the suit, before proceeding to determine the substantive issues raised by the plaintiff. The court held that the NDC failed to comply with the mandatory provisions of the Electoral Act regarding the submission of its membership register to INEC ahead of its primary election. Justice Nganjiwa found that Omo-Agege’s name was not contained in the NDC membership register submitted to INEC at least 21 days before the conduct of the party’s primary election. The judge further held that the NDC failed to provide credible evidence establishing that its membership register was subsequently updated and submitted to INEC within the statutory period preceding the primary. Relying on INEC’s revised electoral timetable, the court also noted that Omo-Agege participated in the APC senatorial primary held on May 18, 2026, a development which, according to the court, established that he was still a member of the APC at the material time. Justice Nganjiwa maintained that only persons whose names appeared in a political party’s membership register, in accordance with the requirements of the Electoral Act, were eligible to participate in its primary elections. On the admissibility of a previously withdrawn affidavit, the court held that a party was entitled to withdraw an affidavit already filed in a proceeding, adding that once withdrawn, such an affidavit ceased to form part of the court’s records and could not be relied upon in determining the matter. The judge maintained that a valid nomination could not be founded on a process that failed to satisfy statutory requirements, stressing that where a political party failed to comply with the Electoral Act in nominating its candidate, INEC was not permitted to include such a candidate on the ballot. Consequently, the court invalidated Omo-Agege’s nomination, directed INEC to delist him and restrained him from presenting himself as the NDC candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the forthcoming general elections. items.title: Binduri MP distributes 1,500 desks to basic schools, promises 500 more
items.description: The Member of Parliament for Binduri, Issifu Mahamoud, has distributed 1,500 mono desks to basic schools across the constituency as part of efforts to address a longstanding shortage of classroom furniture. The MP, who represents the National Democratic Congress (NDC), said the intervention was intended to improve teaching and learning conditions for pupils, some of whom have reportedly had to sit on classroom floors for lessons and written exercises. He disclosed that the distribution forms part of a planned donation of 2,000 desks, with the remaining 500 expected to arrive in the constituency before the end of November 2026. The desks were not ready at the time of the initial distribution, but Mr Mahamoud assured residents that they would be delivered for onward distribution to the beneficiary schools. Mr Mahamoud said improving basic education remained a priority since he assumed office, pointing to other interventions undertaken in schools across the constituency. These include the provision of white marker boards to all junior high schools, the construction of basic school blocks and support for teachers and students at different levels of education. He pledged to continue working to improve educational infrastructure and learning conditions in Binduri before the end of his first term in Parliament. “No child in Binduri should learn on the floor in this modern era,” he said. Chiefs, teachers, parents and pupils have expressed gratitude to the MP for the furniture donation, describing it as an intervention to improve conditions in the beneficiary schools. Mr Mahamoud said investing in children’s education was essential to the constituency’s future. “If we help our children to get better education, we are preparing our own future in a prosperous way,” he emphasised.

items.title: Burkina Faso : Les langues nationales facilitent le dialogue entre soignants et patients à Kokologo
items.description: Après une première étape achevée dans la région du Nakambé, la caravane de presse organisée par le ministère de la Santé, dans le cadre du Mois de la communication sanitaire en langues nationales, a repris son périple à travers les régions du Burkina Faso. Ce 23 novembre 2026, elle a fait escale dans un centre médical de la ville de Kokologo, dans la région du Nando. Il est 8 h 44 au centre médical de Kokologo, ce 23 novembre. Au service de la maternité, les femmes sont déjà présentes pour honorer leurs rendez-vous médicaux. Parmi elles, il y a Fadilatou Kaboré, une femme enceinte de quelques mois. À son tour, elle s’installe dans la salle de consultation. En face d’elle, la sage-femme entame la discussion en mooré, une langue nationale. C’est une pratique qui est devenue courante dans les services de ce centre médical. Conscients que les barrières linguistiques constituent un frein à l’accès aux soins, les professionnels de la santé ont misé sur l’adaptation personnelle. En fonction du patient, l’agent de santé s’attelle à se faire comprendre. Après la consultation, Fadilatou Kaboré s’est réjouie de la procédure. Bien qu’elle s’exprime en français, elle a souhaité avoir les prescriptions médicales en langues nationales pour mieux comprendre. « Lorsque j'étais en consultation, la sage-femme discutait avec moi en mooré. Elle me posait des questions pour connaître l'objet de la consultation. Au fur et à mesure, je répondais à ses questions et elle arrivait à me comprendre. Lorsqu'on échange en mooré, je comprends mieux. La consultation s'est bien passée et j'ai compris les préoccupations de la sage-femme », a-t-elle expliqué. Raïssa Ouérécé/Kaboré, sage-femme au centre médical de Kokologo, a fait preuve d’adaptation depuis son premier poste dans le Sahel. Après avoir eu recours à un interprète pour sensibiliser les femmes, elle s’est décidée à apprendre la langue locale pour être sûre que son message soit bien passé. Le même processus est appliqué au centre de Kokologo. En plus de parler la langue locale, elle n’hésite pas à faire appel à ses collègues lorsqu’il s’agit d’un patient d’une autre ethnie. « À Kokologo, la consultation se fait plus en mooré et le message passe plus facilement. Vu que les femmes comprennent le mooré, quand tu vas vouloir donner des explications en français à une femme qui ne comprend pas, ton message risque de ne pas aller dans le sens que tu voudrais » , a-t-elle indiqué. Le médecin-chef du centre médical de Kokologo, Alassane Ouédraogo, a assuré que dans chaque service, les échanges en langues nationales se déroulent sans difficulté. Il a ajouté qu’il y a beaucoup d’avantages lorsque les agents de santé échangent en langues nationales avec les patients. Cela permet aux professionnels de la santé de mieux faire passer le message et de faire ressortir les détails pendant les sensibilisations. Il a fait comprendre que le Mois de la communication sanitaire en langues nationales a eu un fort impact en matière de mobilisation. À travers la forte fréquentation, ils ont saisi l’occasion pour sensibiliser sur les dangers de certaines maladies comme la dengue, qui a fait des victimes. L’initiative a permis aussi d’effectuer des émissions radiophoniques qui ont enregistré une grande participation des citoyens. « Concernant les émissions à la radio, il y a de la mobilisation et de l'engouement puisqu’on envoie les agents du centre médical en fonction des spécialités. Vous allez voir que pour l'émission sur la dengue c'est essentiellement les médecins qui sont allés, moi et mon collègue. Pour l'émission sur la nutrition, c'était l'attaché de santé qui est allé. Lui aussi, il est spécialiste dans ce domaine. Avec l'engouement, la population est satisfaite. Elle pose des questions pour comprendre. Ils souhaitent qu'on puisse pérenniser ces genres d'initiatives » , a indiqué Alassane Ouédraogo. Pour rappel, le Mois de la communication sanitaire en langues nationales vise à rapprocher davantage l’information sanitaire des populations, en utilisant les langues qu’elles comprennent et dans lesquelles elles s’expriment le mieux. Cheick Habib Désiré BAYILI Faso7 L’article Burkina Faso : Les langues nationales facilitent le dialogue entre soignants et patients à Kokologo est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Caleb Yirenkyi injury ‘awkward to assess’- Coventry manager Frank Lampard
items.description: Coventry head coach Frank Lampard has labelled Caleb Yirenkyi’s injury as an “awkward one to assess” after he missed the English Premier League match against Crystal Palace at the Building Society Arena on Saturday. The Ghanaian midfielder reported to camp at club level with an injury and had to sit on the sidelines in their 3-2 victory. The 21-year-old started for the Black Stars in the 2-0 win over Somalia in the 2027 AFCON qualifier but was not involved in the return fixture. “Caleb has an ankle as well. He came back from Ghana, missed the second game, came back, and he’s got an ankle injury. “We’re going to see how it is. There’s a possibility he’s back for Leeds, but not necessarily. It’s a bit of an awkward one to assess at the minute,” Lampard said. He has made 10 appearances in the Premier League, including eight in the starting line-up. Caleb is, however, expected to be back in action in the coming days ahead of their next encounter against Leeds United on November 28. He joined Coventry during the summer transfer window after shining at the 2026 World Cup, including scoring the decisive goal against Panama, which helped the nation qualify for the Round of 32.

items.title: Africa offers new investment opportunities amid global economic uncertainty – German President
items.description: German President Dr Frank-Walter Steinmeier has urged German businesses to explore investment opportunities in Africa amid growing uncertainty in traditional export markets. He said geopolitical disruptions had weakened the certainty of doing business in major markets such as North America and China, making it important for German companies to consider new opportunities on the African continent. Speaking at the Opening of the Presidential Addresses of the 6th German-African Business Summit in Accra on Tuesday, November 24, he encouraged German businesses to take a greater interest in Africa. “I would urge the German business sector to make use of the opportunities in the African countries. Be curious, take risks, and invest in our common future,” he said. Dr Steinmeier said trade between Germany and African countries increased by about 10 per cent last year to reach a record high, but noted that significant opportunities remained untapped. “However, as all of you also know, there is still much more dormant potential. We are nowhere near where we would be and could be,” he said. He also highlighted the need for African countries to implement reforms, facilitate trade and open new trade routes to strengthen economic cooperation. “Please do not waver in your endeavours to implement necessary reforms and create ways to facilitate trade on your continent and open up new trade routes,” he said. Dr Steinmeier assured African countries that Germany and its businesses were committed to building reliable partnerships. “I can assure you, Germany and German companies are reliable, strong, and transparent partners on this path, actors who keep their word,” the president noted.

items.title: Delta NDC Attack: IPAC warns against bloodshed ahead of 2027 elections
items.description: The Inter-Party Advisory Council (IPAC) has called on the police and other security agencies to investigate the deadly attack on the campaign entourage of Sen. Ovie Omo-Agege in Delta, cautioning against further bloodshed. Mrs Temilola Akinade, Lagos State IPAC Chairperson, made the call while condemning the reported attack on members of Nigeria Democratic Congress. The NDC were on the campaign train of former Deputy Senate President, Omo-Agege, in Uduere Community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of the state when they were reportedly attacked. Omo-Agege is the Delta Central Senatorial candidate of the NDC in 2027 National Assembly elections. Reacting, Akinade, in an interview with Newsmen on Tuesday in Lagos described the incident as a serious threat to democratic participation, political tolerance and the peaceful conduct of political activities in the country. Akinade said: “IPAC considers this development a serious threat to democratic participation, political tolerance and the peaceful conduct of political activities in Nigeria. “We strongly condemn every form of political violence, intimidation, thuggery and the unlawful use of firearms. No political ambition, party affiliation or electoral contest is worth the life of any Nigerian. “IPAC calls on the Inspector-General of Police, the Department of State Services (DSS) and other relevant security agencies to conduct a thorough, independent and transparent investigation into this unfortunate incident and ensure that everyone found culpable, including any sponsors, is brought to justice, irrespective of political affiliation or status.” Akinade also urged the Delta Government to take urgent measures to restore peace, protect lives and property, and guarantee the safety of all political parties and their members across the state. The IPAC chairperson called on political parties, leaders and their supporters to embrace tolerance, peaceful engagement and respect for democratic principles ahead of the 2027 General Elections. She warned against allowing political differences to degenerate into bloodshed, insisting that democracy should be driven by ideas rather than violence. “Democracy must be a contest of ideas, not a battlefield of bullets. Nigeria must not allow political differences to become reasons for bloodshed,” the IPAC boss said. Akinade extended IPAC’s condolences to the bereaved families, the leadership and members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Omo-Agege and the people of Delta State. She also wished those injured in the attack a speedy and complete recovery. The IPAC chair reiterated that every Nigerian had the constitutional right to freedom of association, political participation and peaceful assembly without fear of intimidation or violence. Akinade urged all stakeholders to work towards ensuring that the 2027 elections were conducted in an atmosphere of peace, security and democratic tolerance. items.title: Open up your trade routes – German President tells Africa
items.description: German President Dr Frank-Walter Steinmeier has urged African countries to intensify economic reforms and remove barriers to trade to unlock the continent’s economic potential and strengthen its partnership with Germany. He said African governments must remain committed to implementing necessary reforms, facilitating trade within the continent and opening up new trade routes to promote economic growth and prosperity. “Please do not waver in your endeavours to implement necessary reforms and create ways to facilitate trade on your continent and open up new trade routes,” he said at the 6th German-African Business Summit (GABS 2026) in Accra on Tuesday, November 24. Mr Steinmeier said such measures were essential to expanding economic cooperation between Africa and Germany. “Both things are essential for greater growth and prosperity, as well as for the expansion of our cooperation in our mutual interests,” he added. The German President identified the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) as a crucial step towards achieving greater economic integration and facilitating trade across the continent. “The African Union’s African Continental Free Trade Area, the largest of its kind in the world, is indeed a crucial step here. And it gives me reason for optimism,” he said. He encouraged African countries to pursue the implementation of the continental trade agreement decisively, arguing that greater economic integration would create opportunities for young people and improve their prospects. Mr Steinmeier said economic growth remained central to providing young Africans with better opportunities and a more secure future. “The key to this is economic growth, economic growth that gives young people prospects for a better life,” he stated. He said the German-African Business Summit was important because it provided a platform for establishing business contacts, creating jobs and generating greater prosperity. The President also called on German businesses to take advantage of investment opportunities across Africa, urging them to be more adventurous in exploring the continent’s markets. “I would urge the German business sector to make use of the opportunities in the African countries. Be curious, take risks, and invest in our common future,” he said. He observed that changing geopolitical dynamics had undermined the traditional certainty of major export markets in North America and China for German businesses, making it necessary for companies to explore new economic opportunities in Africa. Mr Steinmeier said trade between Germany and African countries increased by about 10 per cent in 2025, reaching a new record, but stressed that significant untapped potential remained. “However, as all of you also know, there is still much more dormant potential. We are nowhere near where we would be and could be,” he said. The German President further described Germany and its companies as reliable partners for African countries, assuring that they were committed to supporting the continent’s economic development. “I can assure you, Germany and German companies are reliable, strong, and transparent partners on this path, actors who keep their word,” he said. The 6th German-African Business Summit, which runs from November 23 to 25, 2026, is bringing together policymakers, business executives, investors and industry leaders from Germany and across Africa to strengthen economic relations and explore investment opportunities. Discussions at the summit are focusing on energy transition, green hydrogen, digitalisation, artificial intelligence, automotive development, mining, trade finance and industrialisation.

items.title: Le développement de l’entrepreneuriat numérique en Afrique du Nord
items.description: Le capital n’a pas disparu d’Afrique du Nord, mais il circule de manière plus sélective. Au premier semestre 2026, les startups égyptiennes ont levé 158,9 millions de dollars sur 29 opérations, soit 11 % de moins qu’un an plus tôt ; la fintech représentait 82,3 millions de dollars et l’e-commerce 50,2 millions. À l’échelle de la Mena, 1,7 milliard de dollars a été levé sur 242 tours pendant la même période, avec un recul de 28 % du nombre d’opérations. Le filtre s’est resserré. Au Maroc, Digital Morocco 2030 fixe deux objectifs : 240 000 emplois directs dans l’économie numérique et 100 milliards de dirhams de contribution au PIB à l’horizon 2030. La stratégie vise aussi 3 000 startups marocaines labellisées et 7 milliards de dirhams de levées de fonds d'ici 2030. Le 12 juin 2026, la Banque mondiale a approuvé un programme de 250 millions de dollars consacré à la transformation numérique, au cloud, à l’IA, aux PME et au financement des startups. Le passage du prototype au marché devient ainsi le véritable test En Algérie, 1 004 web-marchands étaient raccordés à la plateforme nationale de paiement en ligne à fin juin 2026, contre 644 un an plus tôt. Le premier semestre a compté 15 431 994 paiements en ligne pour 345,58 milliards de dinars ; le GIE Monétique relie les pics de janvier et d’avril aux première et deuxième tranches du programme AADL 3. Dans ce réseau, un site de paris sportifs algérien (arabe : موقع الرهان الرياضي الجزائري ) peut reposer sur les mêmes briques transactionnelles que d’autres services numériques : authentification, comptes clients, paiements électroniques et données en temps réel. Le paiement change l’échelle. Les plateformes transactionnelles exposent le vrai coût du produit Un service numérique qui manipule de l’argent doit gérer le paiement, l’identité, la sécurité, les données et les règles du produit. Dans les paris sportifs, la somme des probabilités implicites dérivées des cotes dépasse généralement 100 % ; cet écart, appelé overround, représente la marge théorique intégrée au marché, tandis qu’un jeu affichant un RTP de 96 % implique un avantage mathématique de la maison de 4 % sur un très grand nombre de parties. Le RTP ne prédit pas une session et la bankroll désigne simplement le capital qu’un joueur décide d’allouer au jeu. Les conditions de mise, les limites, la vérification d’identité et l’historique des transactions doivent être intégrés au produit dès sa conception. La Tunisie dispose, depuis la loi n° 2018-20 du 17 avril 2018, d’un Startup Act structuré autour de 20 mesures et d’un label officiel. AIR prévoit 30 000 dinars tunisiens pour soutenir une preuve de concept, tandis qu’AIR² peut atteindre 200 000 dinars pour des startups ayant déjà levé des fonds seed et préparant une série A. Le fonds de fonds Anava a une taille cible de 100 millions d’euros et vise plus de 13 fonds dédiés aux différentes étapes de développement. Le dispositif relie ainsi le cadre juridique, le financement précoce et le capital-risque. Le Caire construit les rails avant les applications L’Égypte conserve un vaste vivier de talents : ITIDA recense plus de 667 500 diplômés de l’enseignement supérieur par an, dont 37 % dans les filières STEM, et chiffre les exportations numériques à 7,4 milliards de dollars. Depuis le 21 juin 2026, les banques opérant dans le pays utilisent la norme ISO 20022 pour les messages Swift relatifs aux transferts interbancaires. Le 24 août, la Banque centrale a aussi publié les règles de sa plateforme d’identité financière numérique pour l’identification électronique des clients et l’ouverture de comptes à distance. Pour une fintech, ces infrastructures réduisent le nombre de composants bancaires à reconstruire avant de tester un produit. Le troisième trimestre 2026 a vu les startups Mlena lever 1,65 milliard de dollars sur 145 opérations, mais octobre a ramené le total mensuel à 40 millions de dollars. Trois grandes opérations avaient représenté près de 70 % des financements de septembre, tandis qu’en octobre l’Égypte n’a enregistré que 1,7 million de dollars sur six opérations. Pour une entreprise née à Casablanca, Alger, Tunis ou au Caire, l’expansion dépend moins d’un classement ponctuel des levées de fonds que de sa capacité à gérer plusieurs devises, systèmes de paiement et cadres réglementaires. Les revenus récurrents restent un signal plus lisible que la taille d’un seul tour de table. L’article Le développement de l'entrepreneuriat numérique en Afrique du Nord est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: 51 personnes interpellées en 24 heures lors d’opérations de la gendarmerie
items.description: La gendarmerie sénégalaise a interpellé 51 personnes dans la région de Dakar, le 21 novembre 2026, au cours d’opérations ciblant des réseaux d’émigration irrégulière et de trafic de stupéfiants. Les interventions ont également permis la saisie d’une pirogue et de matériel utilisé pour le transport de drogue, selon un communiqué de la Légion de gendarmerie de Dakar. La lutte contre l’émigration clandestine et le trafic de stupéfiants se poursuit au Sénégal. En l’espace de 24 heures, les unités de la gendarmerie ont procédé à l’arrestation de 51 individus dans plusieurs localités de la région de Dakar, à l’issue d’opérations menées le 21 novembre 2026. À Yenne, l’intervention des gendarmes a conduit à l’interpellation de 46 personnes. Parmi elles figurent 42 candidats à l’émigration irrégulière, découverts dans une maison située à Kelle, ainsi que quatre individus soupçonnés d’avoir pris part à l’organisation de leur départ. Deux autres personnes, présumées impliquées dans la préparation d’un voyage clandestin à destination de l’Espagne, ont été arrêtées dans le secteur de Hann. Les forces de sécurité ont également mis la main sur une pirogue qui devait servir à la traversée. Dans la zone de la Foire, deux individus suspectés d’organiser un départ irrégulier ont également été appréhendés. Selon les premiers éléments de l’enquête, ils auraient recruté quatre candidats à l’émigration et mobilisé des fonds destinés à financer leur voyage. Parallèlement, les opérations contre le trafic de drogue ont permis l’arrestation d’un individu à Keur Massar. Celui-ci détenait 53 cornets de kush. Une motocyclette présumée utilisée pour le transport et la livraison de cette substance a également été saisie. À l’issue de ces différentes interventions, les enquêtes se poursuivent au sein des unités compétentes de la gendarmerie. Elles visent à établir les responsabilités des personnes interpellées et à remonter d’éventuelles ramifications des réseaux concernés. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article 51 personnes interpellées en 24 heures lors d’opérations de la gendarmerie est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: France : la députée Sabrina Sebaihi dénonce une série de fermetures de structures musulmanes
items.description: En France, le climat islamophobe s'accentue de jour en jour. Dénoncée à maintes reprises par la Grande Mosquée de Paris et son recteur Chems-Eddine Hafiz, cette islamophobie rampante vient de frapper encore une fois. La députée Sabrina Sebaihi alerte sur la multiplication des « actes islamophobes et racistes ». À Nanterre, dans le département des Hauts-de-Seine, l'école musulmane Ibn Badis vient de faire l’objet d’une mesure préfectorale. Un arrêté préfectoral contesté en justice Dans un communiqué publié le 21 novembre 2026, l’Institut Ibn Badis a annoncé avoir reçu un arrêté préfectoral lui interdisant l’accueil des mineurs dans le cadre de ses activités extrascolaires. Cette décision fait suite à un contrôle du Service départemental à la jeunesse, à l’engagement et aux sports (SDJES). L’établissement conteste cette mesure et annonce, par l’intermédiaire de son avocat, Maître Guez Guez, la saisine du tribunal administratif en référé. Au cœur du différend figure la qualification de ses activités. Alors que la préfecture les considère comme relevant de la réglementation des accueils collectifs de mineurs (ACM), l’institut estime qu’elles relèvent principalement de l’enseignement et de la transmission religieuse. La députée Sabrina Sebaihi appelle au dialogue Dans un communiqué publié lundi 23 novembre, Sabrina Sebaihi, députée de Nanterre-Suresnes, a exprimé son soutien à l’établissement, à ses équipes et aux familles concernées. Elle déplore que de nombreux enfants « soient privés de leurs cours » du jour au lendemain, rappelant les trente années d’engagement de l’Institut auprès des habitants de Nanterre. L’élue évoque également une succession de « fermetures de structures musulmanes », notamment à « Colombes, Décines et Alès ». S’adressant au préfet des Hauts-de-Seine, elle estime que « le dialogue doit primer » et lui demande de recevoir les responsables de l’établissement afin de trouver une solution permettant une reprise rapide des activités. « Les actes islamophobes et racistes se multiplient, et des mosquées sont prises pour cibles. Dans le même temps, les fermetures de structures musulmanes se succèdent : Colombes, Décines, Alès, et maintenant Nanterre », a-t-elle alerté. Un rassemblement annoncé le 28 novembre Parallèlement aux démarches judiciaires, l’Institut Ibn Badis appelle à un rassemblement pacifique et solidaire, prévu le samedi 28 novembre 2026 à 12 heures, devant ses locaux, au 227-231 avenue Georges-Clemenceau, à Nanterre . À travers cette mobilisation, organisée sous le slogan « Nous ne lâcherons rien », l'établissement entend réclamer la levée de l'interdiction des cours extrascolaires et défendre les droits des enfants et des familles. Le président de l'Institut, Rachid Abdouni, assure que la structure poursuivra ses recours juridiques et défendra sa mission éducative. items.title: Burkina Faso : l’UEMOA veut encadrer l’essor des satellites en orbite basse
items.description: L'essor des constellations de satellites en orbite basse (LEO) s'impose comme un nouvel enjeu pour les politiques numeriques de l'Union economique et monetaire ouest-africaine (UEMOA). Reunis a Ouagadougou du 23 au 26 novembre, les participants a la 17e Assemblee generale de la Conference des operateurs et fournisseurs de services de telecommunications des etats membres (COFTEL) ont appele a integrer ces nouvelles technologies sans fragiliser les investissements realises dans les infrastructures terrestres. Responsables politiques, regulateurs et operateurs ont debattu des conditions d'une concurrence equitable entre les differents acteurs, ainsi que des moyens d'etendre l'acces a internet dans les zones mal desservies. Les perturbations provoquees en mars 2024 par la coupure simultanee de quatre câbles sous-marins au large de la Cote d'Ivoire ont illustre la vulnerabilite des infrastructures de telecommunications africaines. Treize pays avaient alors ete touches, dont cinq membres de l'UEMOA : le Benin, le Burkina Faso, la Cote d'Ivoire, le Niger et le Togo. Le Niger a pu maintenir certains services essentiels grâce aux connexions satellitaires et aux liaisons terrestres passant par le Burkina Faso et le Benin. « Aucune technologie ne tient seule », a rappele Guynand Maxime-Thierry Kouame, directeur de cabinet a la Commission de l'UEMOA. Les besoins en matiere de connectivite restent considerables. Selon les donnees de la GSMA presentees lors des travaux, 9 % de la population africaine vit dans des zones depourvues de couverture mobile a haut debit. Par ailleurs, 63 % des Africains vivent dans des zones couvertes par un reseau mobile a haut debit mais n'utilisent pas l'internet mobile, notamment en raison du coût des equipements et des forfaits, ainsi que du manque de competences numeriques. Souverainete numerique et equite reglementaire Au Burkina Faso, les autorites ont insiste sur la necessite de maîtriser les infrastructures, les donnees et les technologies. Representant la ministre de la Transition digitale, Nongobzanga Zongo, directeur de la Communication electronique, a rappele que « la souverainete numerique ne se decrete pas », mais repose sur la maîtrise des infrastructures et des competences. Les autorites ont egalement mis en garde contre une ouverture du marche susceptible de fragiliser les operateurs locaux et de compromettre leurs investissements. En 2024, le Burkina Faso comptait 11 291 kilometres de fibre optique, tandis que la Cote d'Ivoire disposait de plus de 30 000 kilometres de fibre et de cinq câbles sous-marins. Pour Boris Compaore, directeur general de Telecel Faso et president sortant de la COFTEL, les reseaux terrestres et satellitaires doivent etre complementaires plutot que concurrents. Les operateurs satellitaires devraient toutefois respecter des obligations comparables a celles imposees aux acteurs terrestres, notamment en matiere de licences, de fiscalite, de contribution au service universel, de protection des donnees et de cybersecurite. Les satellites en orbite basse offrent en effet la possibilite de fournir un acces a internet a haut debit dans les territoires enclaves, ou le deploiement de la fibre optique ou des reseaux mobiles s'avere particulierement coûteux. Vers un reseau satellitaire communautaire Dans cette perspective, la Commission de l'UEMOA prevoit de recruter, au debut de 2027, un cabinet charge d'etudier la faisabilite d'un reseau satellitaire propre a l'espace communautaire. L'etude devra notamment permettre d'evaluer les conditions techniques, economiques et reglementaires d'un tel projet. La 17e Assemblee generale a egalement ete marquee par le changement de presidence de la COFTEL. Apres deux annees a la tete de l'organisation, Telecel Faso doit ceder la presidence a Airtel Niger, qui aura notamment pour mission de poursuivre les travaux d'harmonisation reglementaire entre les etats membres.

items.title: Sales tax zones being established in Karachi, Lahore, Islamabad and Multan, PM told
items.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif was informed on Tuesday that separate sales tax zones were being established in the country’s four major taxpayer units — Karachi, Lahore, Islamabad and Multan — to improve collection. According to a statement from the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), the development was shared during a weekly review meeting concerning the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) in Islamabad. The move comes as the government has decided to reverse the functional integration of sales tax and income tax collection after 17 years, acknowledging that the sales tax revenue gap has widened to Rs3.4 trillion amid weak enforcement and poor revenue collection. The statement released on Tuesday said that the meeting was also informed that work was underway to establish a modern cargo tracking system to address the sales tax gap and curb smuggling. The system would digitally track the movement of goods from loading to delivery and comprise an electronic consignment note, a risk management system, field enforcement and an analytics dashboard, the statement said. A steering committee with provincial representation was also being formed to oversee the system’s implementation, the PMO said. The meeting was further informed that the FBR was establishing an office at Karachi’s Korangi Industrial Estate to provide services to local industrialists at their doorstep. According to the PMO, PM Shehbaz directed authorities to expedite customs clearance, immigration and other operations at the country’s airports and make smart scanning systems operational at all international airports. The meeting was informed that smart scanning systems were being installed at major international airports with the support of relevant agencies. The systems would automatically direct passengers’ baggage to the green or red channels. The prime minister expressed the hope that the FBR chairman’s recent visits to Karachi and Lahore and meetings with local traders and industrialists would yield positive results for trade, exports and investment. The meeting was informed that an audit of oil marketing companies’ bonded warehouses, conducted on the prime minister’s directives, had uncovered irregularities amounting to Rs24.4 billion. Recoveries were being made through legal procedures, the statement said. It added that PM Shehbaz directed authorities to take action and make recoveries without discrimination. The meeting was further informed that the Indus Collectorate had begun operations at bridges over the Indus River across the country. The enforcement collectorate, which had 856 staff members, had seized illegal goods worth Rs1.849bn in 302 operations so far, the statement said. Regarding Pakistan Revenue Automation Limited (PRAL), the meeting was informed that additional security features had been incorporated into several software systems to ensure data integrity. Departmental action was also being taken against FBR officers who had previously issued unauthorised consumption certificates under the FATA/PATA tax exemption, the statement said. In 2009, the government transferred the administration of sales tax and federal excise duty from Customs to the Inland Revenue Service (IRS) as part of a World Bank-backed reform aimed at integrating tax administration. However, after 17 years of integration, the sales tax revenue gap has widened to an estimated Rs3.4tr, compared with Rs2tr for income tax, raising questions about the effectiveness of the arrangement. Under the new arrangement, specialised officers will handle sales tax and income tax separately, while both will continue to be administered within the IRS rather than through separate services.

items.title: GES warns parents; says 2-year exam ban for early BECE, WASSCE candidates will be enforced
items.description: The Ghana Education Service (GES) has warned that candidates who sit the Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE) or the West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE) ahead of their officially approved examination periods will be barred from taking the respective examination for two years. The directive, contained in a letter dated November 23, 2026, follows a warning by the Minister for Education, Haruna Iddrisu, at the launch of the 2026 National Education Week at the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC). Under the directive, any candidate who writes either examination ahead of the approved schedule will face a two-year ban from taking that examination. The GES has consequently instructed all Regional Directors of Education to ensure strict compliance with the directive and communicate it to Metropolitan, Municipal and District Directors of Education, heads of schools and other relevant stakeholders within their jurisdictions. The announcement follows concerns raised by Mr Iddrisu over the practice of some parents pushing their children to sit the BECE before their expected year of completion. Speaking at the National Education Week launch, the Minister specifically cautioned Junior High School (JHS) One and Two pupils against advancing to JHS Three prematurely to write the examination ahead of schedule. He explained that the measure was intended to instil discipline in the education system, promote fairness and enable education authorities to accurately determine the number of pupils expected to complete basic education and sit the BECE each year. Mr Iddrisu also argued that allowing some children to write the examination ahead of their peers, often due to parental pressure, undermined equity and equal opportunities within the education system. The GES directive is expected to reinforce the Minister’s position by ensuring that candidates adhere to the officially approved examination timelines for both the BECE and WASSCE. The Service is counting on education officials and school authorities to ensure the directive is effectively communicated and enforced across the country.

items.title: France : 15 pertes de grossesse signalées après une exposition aux gaz lacrymogènes
items.description: « J'ai perdu mon bebe apres sept mois de grossesse », temoigne une femme. Elle promenait son chien lorsqu'elle a ete exposee aux gaz lacrymogenes. Le 17 novembre, le collectif Lacrymos de sang a presente son enquete a l'Assemblee nationale. Sur les 9 480 temoignages analyses, neuf femmes sur dix font etat de troubles gynecologiques. Dans la moitie des cas, il s'est ecoule moins de douze heures avant l'apparition des premiers symptomes. Les crampes uterines reviennent le plus souvent dans les temoignages (59 %), suivies des douleurs ovariennes (43 %). 25 % des femmes evoquent des saignements inhabituellement abondants. Parmi les 47 femmes enceintes exposees, quinze signalent une perte de grossesse. Des risques sanitaires longtemps negliges Le CS, principal agent actif des gaz lacrymogenes, se degrade dans l'organisme, produisant notamment une substance susceptible d'activer certains recepteurs impliques dans la perception de la douleur et de l'irritation. Ces recepteurs sont egalement presents dans l'endometre, la muqueuse qui tapisse l'uterus. Les chercheurs interroges par Mediapart avancent une hypothese : les produits issus de la degradation du CS pourraient atteindre cette muqueuse et y declencher une reaction inflammatoire. Mais sur quelles donnees repose l'evaluation des risques pour les femmes ? « Les rares etudes de toxicologie sur le gaz CS datent d'il y a plus de trente ans et portent uniquement sur des sujets mâles ! », pointe Solenne Rougeux, doctorante en neuroendocrinologie a l'universite Paris-Saclay, dans Mediapart. La composition exacte des produits utilises par la police francaise demeure par ailleurs confidentielle. 22 000 grenades en une journee Les alertes ne datent pourtant pas d'hier. En 2023, des chercheurs americains avaient etudie le cas de 1 276 personnes exposees aux agents chimiques employes par les forces de l'ordre. Parmi elles, 83 % avaient signale des troubles de la sante reproductive. Lors des manifestations du 17 octobre , les forces de l'ordre francaises ont fait usage de quelque 22 000 grenades lacrymogenes, selon un chiffre communique aux deputes le 3 novembre par le ministre de l'Interieur, Laurent Nuñez. Le 1er decembre 2018, au plus fort de la mobilisation des Gilets jaunes, 7 940 grenades avaient ete utilisees, soit un peu plus du tiers de ce nombre, d'apres Le Monde . Quatre deputes de La France insoumise (LFI) ont depose une proposition de loi visant a interdire l'usage des gaz lacrymogenes lors des manifestations. Le collectif invoque le principe de precaution pour en demander la suspension. Les autorites francaises continuent, elles, de recourir a ces substances alors que leurs effets sur la sante gynecologique restent insuffisamment etudies.

items.title: 72 heures de l’Assurance 2026 : L’APSAB outille les journalistes sur les enjeux de l’assurance vie
items.description: Dans le cadre des 72 heures de l’assurance 2026, l’Association professionnelle des sociétés d’assurance du Burkina (APSAB) a organisé, ce 23 novembre à Ouagadougou, une session de formation à l’intention des journalistes. Cette initiative vise à renforcer leurs connaissances sur l’assurance vie et à faire des médias des relais d’une information plus accessible aux populations. Prévoir les imprévus, préparer sa retraite et assurer l’avenir de ses proches. L’assurance vie offre plusieurs possibilités de protection financière. Pourtant, ses mécanismes et ses avantages restent encore méconnus d’une partie de la population. C’est pour contribuer à une meilleure compréhension de cette branche que l’APSAB a réuni des professionnels des médias autour d’une session de formation, ce lundi 23 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou. Pour Marie Batiénon, directrice générale adjointe de UAB Assurance Vie, vice-présidente de l’APSAB et superviseure de la commission technique vie, cette initiative répond à un déficit de connaissance constaté auprès des populations. Elle estime que de nombreux Burkinabè ne maîtrisent pas encore suffisamment les principes de l’assurance, particulièrement ceux de l’assurance vie. « C’est de notre responsabilité de sensibiliser nos frères et sœurs et c’est cette dynamique que nous avons voulu enclencher en organisant cette session de formation », a-t-elle expliqué. Cette démarche s’inscrit dans une stratégie de sensibilisation plus large. Elle prévoit notamment des interventions sur les plateaux médiatiques pour mieux informer les citoyens. À l’ouverture des travaux, la responsable a également souligné la portée sociale de l’assurance vie. Elle a plaidé pour une meilleure appropriation de cet outil par les populations. « L’assurance vie devrait être comprise par tous et adoptée par tous. C’est un acte d’amour envers ceux qu’on aime et envers soi-même » , a-t-elle déclaré. Elle a, dans ce sens, invité les journalistes à contribuer à sa vulgarisation auprès du public. L’assurance vie, un levier de protection et de financement La session technique a été animée par Clément Sanwidi, directeur général de Coris Assurance Vie. Son intervention a notamment permis de mettre en lumière la contribution de l’assurance vie au développement économique. À travers la collecte de l’épargne, les compagnies d’assurance mobilisent des ressources susceptibles de participer au financement de l’économie nationale. Pour les souscripteurs, cette branche présente également plusieurs avantages. Selon le formateur, elle permet d’anticiper les besoins liés à la retraite, de constituer une épargne destinée aux études des enfants et de préserver la sécurité financière de la famille. Elle prévoit aussi des garanties en cas de décès ou d’invalidité absolue et définitive. Évoquant le rapport des Burkinabè à l’assurance, Clément Sanwidi relève un intérêt des populations pour ce secteur. Il estime toutefois que cet intérêt gagnerait à se traduire par une adhésion plus importante. Pour lui, les médias constituent des partenaires essentiels pour faire connaître les différentes offres et les garanties proposées par les sociétés d’assurance. Du côté des participants, les échanges ont permis de mieux cerner les implications de l’assurance vie. Jean-François Somé, journaliste à Minute.bf, retient particulièrement son rôle dans la préparation de l’avenir des enfants et la protection des familles. Il a également relevé la persistance de certains préjugés. Parmi eux, l’idée que l’assurance serait un service essentiellement destiné aux personnes nanties. « Au sortir de cette formation, nous sommes outillés et, en tant qu’hommes de médias, nous sommes prêts à relayer l’information juste auprès de nos populations afin de sensibiliser et aussi mobiliser, encourager les personnes à se faire assurer » , a-t-il affirmé. Cette rencontre a également marqué le lancement des activités des 72 heures de l’assurance 2026. Elle s’est achevée par une remise symbolique d’attestations de participation aux journalistes. Selon Marie Batiénon, le programme se poursuivra avec des émissions radiophoniques et télévisuelles, une conférence de presse ainsi que d’autres activités de sensibilisation. Un gala est également prévu pour marquer la clôture de cette édition. À travers ces différentes initiatives, l’APSAB entend contribuer à une meilleure connaissance de l’assurance et encourager les populations à s’intéresser davantage aux solutions de protection qu’elle propose. Éléonore Savadogo Faso7 L’article 72 heures de l’Assurance 2026 : L’APSAB outille les journalistes sur les enjeux de l’assurance vie est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Burkina Faso : Orange Burkina récompense les lauréats de l’Orange Summer Challenge (OSC) 2026
items.description: L'édition 2026 de l’Orange Summer Challenge (OSC) a connu son apothéose, ce 19 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou. La cérémonie a été marquée par la remise des prix aux membres de quatre équipes porteuses de projets innovants et structurels. Le premier prix de cette édition a été remporté par les porteurs du projet Vexdrone. C'est une solution d'intelligence artificielle conçue pour détecter des anomalies sur les infrastructures électriques en faisant usage de drones. Selon les concepteurs, elle est avantageuse en ce sens qu'elle va faciliter l'inspection des infrastructures électriques et permettre aux techniciens des compagnies d'électricité de réduire le temps d'inspection en cas de panne. En guise de récompense, Orange Burkina leur a offert des équipements d'une valeur de 4 millions de FCFA. « Vraiment, on se sent heureux, on se sent vraiment heureux face à une telle situation quand on regarde un peu le parcours pendant 3 mois, les difficultés qu'on a surmontées, ça fait vraiment plaisir. Mais en même temps, c'est un challenge parce que ça ne s'arrête pas là. Nous devons représenter le Burkina Faso à l'échelle internationale » , s'est réjoui Zozerigué Traoré, porte-parole de l'équipe. L'équipe de Shango, lauréate du deuxième prix a reçu des équipements d'une valeur de 3 millions FCFA. C'est un projet de détection de pannes sur les infrastructures de l'énergie solaire. Les lauréats du troisième prix reçoivent un chèque de 2,5 millions FCFA en équipement et la quatrième équipe s'en sort avec un chèque de 2 millions de FCFA en équipement. L'édition 2026 de l'OSC s'est tenue sous le thème : « l’intelligence artificielle comme levier de croissance pour les entreprises ». Ce sont au total 200 candidatures qui ont été enregistrées. À l'issue de la phase de sélection, 20 jeunes talents ont poursuivi l'aventure pendant plusieurs semaines. Cette compétition constitue l'une des actions concrètes d'Orange Burkina en faveur de la vision du Burkina Faso en matière de technologie. Le pays veut faire de la technologie un levier de développement capable d'apporter des réponses concrètes face aux défis actuels. La représentante de la Directrice générale d'Orange Burkina, Alimata Toure/ Yao a ajouté que cette édition s'inscrit en droite ligne de la feuille de route nationale qui fait vœu de faire de l’intelligence artificielle un outil au service des besoins des populations. « Orange a fait de l'Afrique et du Moyen-Orient l'un des moteurs de sa stratégie Trust The Future. Sur un continent dont l'âge moyen avoisine 20 ans, notre conviction est simple : la jeunesse africaine est le premier atout du continent et investir sur ses compétences est l'investissement le plus rentable qui soit pour notre pays comme pour notre entreprise », a-t-elle ajouté. Également, Orange Burkina s'est fixé pour objectif la formation de plus de 3 millions de jeunes d'ici 2030 aux métiers de l'intelligence artificielle, de la cybersécurité, du cloud ainsi que de l'entrepreneuriat numérique. L’entreprise ambitionne aussi de porter à 100 le nombre de ses Orange Digital en Afrique et au Moyen-Orient. Outre cela, en 2026, plus de 12 000 jeunes ont bénéficié des programmes gratuits. Pour la seule année 2026, près de 5 000 jeunes ont été formés et accompagnés. Présent à la cérémonie, le ministre secrétaire général de la présidence du Faso, le Pr Zakaria Soré a salué Orange Burkina pour son rôle de valorisation de la jeunesse. Il a apprécié à sa juste valeur les jeunes talents pour leur sens de la créativité et de l’innovation. Il s'est réjoui de savoir qu'ils mettent en place des projets pour relever les défis existentiels des populations et des entreprises. Cheick Habib Désiré BAYILI Faso7 L’article Burkina Faso : Orange Burkina récompense les lauréats de l’Orange Summer Challenge (OSC) 2026 est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: The exam hall is teaching Ghana the wrong lesson
items.description: Every year, more than 600,000 Ghanaian children sit the BECE. In 2025 the figure was 603,328 candidates from 20,395 schools . Few of them know that their grades are not purely a measure of what they learned. WAEC uses stanine grading, which ranks candidates relative to one another . The top grade is aimed at roughly the best 4% nationwide, so a child who is first in her school may still miss it . Before they turn 15, we have taught them a lesson: your success depends on someone else’s failure. I have watched this play out in our classrooms and our Parliament, and I am convinced it starts early. Colonial rule made ranking and selection the backbone of our schools, and that habit now shapes our politics too. Our own inheritance points the other way, and I believe the classroom is where we must start to reclaim it. Let me be careful with the word “competition”. There is competition for play: I enjoy watching the Black Stars beat an opponent, or two rappers trade bars. There is competition with yourself: being better today than yesterday, as our parents taught us. And there is the competition I reject: making a child’s future depend on outranking other children, so that one person’s rise requires another’s fall. In trade, our ancestors spoke of exchange; in craft, of distinction. The Kente weaver did not need to defeat the Adinkra maker. But when it comes to building a nation, we rise together or not at all. Built to Find Clerks, Not Citizens Long before the colonial school, a Gold Coast child was raised by the whole village. Children learned history, music, rhetoric and survival in groups, often by age grade . No child was ranked against another at grandmother’s evening story time. The colonial government wanted something else: workers for its offices. In 1914 it ran only 8% of Gold Coast schools . It invested mainly in schools that produced junior cadres for administration and commerce. As colonial rule grew, so did demand for clerks, messengers and interpreters . From 1910, British examination boards were invited into colonial Africa to test and select them. This is where our exam culture was born. A small number of positions existed, so the system’s job was to rank and filter. The few who passed served the empire, often in isolation from their communities. The many who failed were told they were not good enough. The British left in 1957, but the exam hall they built is still standing, and we have rarely stopped to ask whose purpose it serves. But we cannot lay all of this at the colonial master’s door. Ghana has had 69 years to rebuild that hall, and successive governments have chosen to keep it. What the Nnoboa Farm Knew Long before anyone lectured us about teamwork, Akan farmers had nnoboa , a customary arrangement of reciprocal labour exchange for farm work , mainly weeding. Today I work on your farm; tomorrow you work on mine. Researchers still argue that this ethic can strengthen resilience in African farming . The same logic lives in communal labour days, the extended family and the Southern African idea of Ubuntu: a person is a person through other people. Ask any elder from a farming town what happened to the man who fell behind. Nobody left his weeds standing. He was not ranked and dropped. His field was weeded with everyone else’s, and he owed his labour back. That is how a village stays fed. Rwanda has taken the same idea national. On the last Saturday of every month, Umuganda brings citizens together for projects of common good, followed by open dialogue with local leaders. The president and Cabinet join in too . Today the state has instituted it by law for adults aged 18 to 65 , turning an old tradition into a national norm. The lesson for Ghana is that togetherness lasts when the community owns it, as nnoboa farmers always did. Monday’s Lesson, Exam Day’s Reality Some will call this romance about the village. Yet decades of research, across hundreds of studies , find that children learn more working together than racing each other. And we need not travel far for examples. Kenya banned the ranking of schools and candidates in national exams to end cut-throat competition, and its new competency-based assessments do not produce aggregate scores to rank learners . Mauritius abolished ranking at its primary exam and now admits children to secondary school regionally, weighing how close they live . Neither system is perfect, but both are African proof that a nation can stop racing its children. Ghana already knows this on paper. The 2019 Standards-Based Curriculum lists communication and collaboration among six core competencies. Yet critics say classrooms look almost identical to a decade ago . We tell children to work together on Monday, then on exam day we line them up against each other. Children are not fools; they follow what we reward. The cost shows up as cheating. WAEC stopped publishing school league tables because malpractice rose whenever they appeared . Then comes placement. GES sorts senior high schools into Categories A, B and C, and every September parents fight over a handful of famous names. This year, Category C schools declared 468,652 vacancies, yet only 123,577 candidates chose them first . Students in Category C schools report that their teachers see them as less intelligent . The government’s answer is to upgrade more schools to Category A . The better answer is a national plan to build and equip good schools in every district, with equal teachers and tools in every region. Education is not for one class of children with one type of grade; it is for everyone. When every community has enough good schools, nobody needs a ranking to find a seat, and a child can learn, live and serve in her own community. Some will object that boarding schools far from home bring Ghanaians of every region and tribe together. That matters. But teacher postings, student exchanges and national service can build that unity without uprooting 14-year-olds from their communities. From the Exam Hall to Parliament House The same reward-the-winner logic runs from our exam halls to our Parliament. In Ghana’s winner-takes-all politics, a predecessor’s project is often treated as an opponent’s trophy. In May 2026, the DACF Administrator said Ghana has close to GH¢8 billion in unfinished projects , partly due to politics and partly because the money was not there. Both parties carry this. After 2017, the $339 million Euroget district hospitals begun under the NDC stalled. Today the NPP Minority claims over 80% of 1,000+ inherited road projects have been abandoned. NDC or NPP, the pattern is the same, and it is the ordinary Ghanaian who pays for the unfinished hospital. The same fate meets our long-term plans. The NDPC chairman, Dr Nii Moi Thompson, lists the 40-Year Plan, Ghana Beyond Aid and Vision 2057 among initiatives brushed aside. He warns that Ghana, stuck in a “middle-income trap” since 2010 , risks staying there unless Parliament adopts a consolidated national plan. Look at Kenya. After the disputed 2007 election, opponents formed a Grand Coalition and adopted one long-term plan, Vision 2030 . Later governments bent it towards their own manifestos , which is exactly why Ghana’s plan must be protected by law. Germany does something similar: parties negotiate coalition agreements of up to 177 pages and then vote together to deliver them. Even opponents can sit at one table when the nation is at stake. Parties may differ in their ideas, but they should reason together on how to build, and never tear down what the nation has already started. The Left Hand Washes the Right So here is where I would start, with five changes to move us from “I” to “we”: Assess against standards, not each other. Grade BECE and WASSCE on whether a child met the curriculum standard, and place children in good schools near home, not by rank. Grade group work for real. Make nnoboa -style team projects a scored part of continuous assessment, with each member accountable. Let our beloved quiz shows evolve too, from “who knows the most?” to “which schools, working together, can solve a real community problem?” Reward schools for lifting the weakest. Measure progress, not just top scores, so strong schools gain by supporting weak ones, and phase out the A, B, C categories by levelling up every school. Make the national plan bind every government. Give a consolidated plan cross-party backing in Parliament, including enough good schools in every district, and require public costing before any project is abandoned. Teach our own models. Put nnoboa , communal labour and Ubuntu into civic education, so our children learn to live them. Picture a classroom where the child who understands the sum turns to explain it to the one who does not. Both walk out stronger. Now picture that habit in our district assemblies and in Parliament. Our elders said benkum dware nifa, na nifa dware benkum: the left hand washes the right, and the right washes the left. A nation that forgets this will keep scrubbing alone. Creppy Emmanuel is an AI Governance Consultant, Digital Strategist, and Cultural Diplomat based in Accra, Ghana, writing on the intersection of African philosophy, governance, and technology.

items.title: Mayweather gives JoySports’ Nathaniel Attoh glowing endorsement in Ghana
items.description: American boxing legend Floyd Mayweather Jr has praised JoySports broadcaster and ring announcer Nathaniel Attoh for his skills following their interactions during the former world champion’s visit to Ghana. Mayweather, who arrived in the country on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, embarked on a series of engagements with Ghanaian personalities, traditional authorities and members of the country’s boxing fraternity. Attoh played a prominent role throughout the visit, serving as the announcer responsible for introducing the undefeated American at several of his engagements. It was during one of those interactions that the five-division world champion acknowledged Attoh’s work, telling him: “You’re good at what you do.” Mayweather’s Ghana itinerary included a courtesy visit to President John Dramani Mahama, a meeting with Ga Mantse King Tackie Teiko Tsuru II at the Ga Mantse Palace and engagements with prominent figures in the country’s boxing community. He also visited the Bronx Boxing Gym in Jamestown, where he interacted with local fighters and trainer Carl Lokko, before making an appearance at the Bukom Boxing Arena. The American also met some of Ghana’s boxing personalities, including three-time world champion Azumah Nelson. For Attoh, however, the visit provided another opportunity to demonstrate his experience as a ring announcer on an international stage. Announcing the exhibition bout between the legendary Azumah Nelson and the then EU Ambassador to Ghana Irchad Razaaly A licensed ring announcer of the Ghana Boxing Authority (GBA), currently operating under an Interim Management Committee, Attoh has announced some of the biggest fight nights in Ghana and on the continent. His work has featured on SuperSport broadcasts reaching audiences in more than 40 countries, while his experience has also seen him announce events attended by heavyweight boxing star Anthony Joshua and global music icon Davido. Beyond announcing, Attoh has established himself as a respected boxing journalist, interviewing some of the sport’s most influential figures, including Hall of Fame boxer Oscar De La Hoya, legendary promoter Don King and Top Rank founder Bob Arum. He has also covered training camps involving several of Ghana’s former world champions, including Azumah Nelson, Ike Bazooka Quartey, Joshua Clottey, Joseph Agbeko, Isaac Dogboe, Richard Commey and Emmanuel Tagoe. His contributions to boxing storytelling extend to documentary production, with notable works including The Boxing Loan, which chronicles Ghana’s first world boxing champion D.K. Poison, Return of the Royal Storm, focusing on former WBO super-bantamweight champion Isaac Dogboe, and Olympic Boxing Genes, documenting the remarkable story of the three Samir brothers who represented Ghana at the Olympic Games. Interviewing the legendary D.K. Poison during the production of The Boxing Loan Documentary

items.title: DR Congo: Gavi signs agreement with Serum Institute of India to secure rapid access to Bundibugyo vaccines
items.description: Country: Democratic Republic of the Congo Source: GAVI Alliance Advance purchase commitment from Gavi secures access to up to 1.5 million doses of ChAdOx1 BDBV, a Bundibugyo candidate vaccine developed jointly by Serum Institute of India and the Oxford Vaccine Group at the University of Oxford The agreement is funded through Gavi’s First Response Fund, with supply remaining conditional on clinical trial results, as well as the candidate vaccine securing necessary regulatory approvals and policy recommendations Dr Sania Nishtar, CEO of Gavi: “For the second public health emergency of international concern since its launch, the First Response Fund is functioning as designed – securing early and rapid access to vaccines so that communities can be protected as quickly as possible.” Geneva, 24 November 2026 – Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance today announced that it had signed an advance purchase commitment with the Serum Institute of India (SII) and Serum Life Sciences to secure access to up to 1.5 million doses of ChAdOx1 BDBV – a candidate vaccine against the Bundibugyo species of Ebolavirus. These doses, funded through Gavi’s First Response Fund * (FRF), would be procured in the event of successful clinical trial results, regulatory approvals, and appropriate policy recommendations for the vaccine’s use. “For the second public health emergency of international concern since its launch, the First Response Fund is functioning as designed – securing early and rapid access to vaccines so that communities can be protected as quickly as possible,” said Dr Sania Nishtar, CEO of Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance. “As the Ebola outbreak continues to devastate communities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, we must act with urgency to ensure the regulatory pathways are in place to quickly roll out this vaccine candidate if the clinical trials show positive results. This is critical to saving lives and keeping the world safe.” To date, the current Ebola outbreak has resulted in more than 11,600 cases and more than 5,700 deaths – the vast majority in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. ChAdOx1 BDBV is one of two novel Bundibugyo vaccine candidates that WHO has recommended for clinical testing in the on-going outbreak. In the event that the candidate vaccine secures the necessary regulatory approvals and WHO SAGE policy recommendations following its trials, Gavi’s advance purchase commitment means that doses can be made available to affected populations quickly. SII has already manufactured the drug substance for more than half a million doses of the candidate vaccine to enable rapid access. Today’s announcement is part of Gavi’s overall support for the response to the on-going Ebola outbreak. Up to US$ 40 million from the First Response Fund (FRF) mechanism has been dedicated to support vaccine access deals such as this advance purchase commitment. An additional US$ 10 million from the FRF – of which US$ 6 million has already been committed or disbursed to the DRC, Uganda, Africa CDC, WHO and UNICEF – is helping to protect routine immunisation services in impacted communities and frontline health workers. Ervebo, an existing Ebola vaccine which is licensed for use against the Ebola Zaire strain of the disease, is also being deployed under clinical research protocols. Gavi has made an additional investment of US$7 million to provide 70,000 doses of the existing Ervebo from the Gavi-funded global stockpile. These doses are currently being administered to affected populations in the DRC under WHO compassionate emergency use protocols. Notes to Editors *The First Response Fund (FRF) is made possible by the governments that have invested in this crucial part of Gavi’s outbreak and pandemic response capacity. Gavi recognises the critical support of the United States, Japan, Italy, Germany, Norway and France , whose commitments helped to ensure Gavi’s $500m FRF was fully funded. The FRF was also leveraged to rapidly respond to the 2024 Mpox emergency. Read more here . About Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance is a public-private partnership that helps vaccinate more than half the world’s children against some of the world’s deadliest diseases. The Vaccine Alliance brings together developing country and donor governments, the World Health Organization, UNICEF, the World Bank, the vaccine industry, technical agencies, civil society, the Gates Foundation and other private sector partners. View the full list of donor governments and other leading organisations that fund Gavi’s work here . Since its inception in 2000, Gavi has helped to immunise a whole generation – over 1.3 billion children – and prevented more than 23 million future deaths, helping to halve child mortality in 78 lower income countries. Gavi also plays a key role in improving global health security by supporting health systems as well as funding global stockpiles for Ebola, cholera, meningococcal, mpox and yellow fever vaccines. After more than two decades of progress, Gavi is now focused on protecting the next generation, above all the zero-dose children who have not received even a single vaccine shot. The Vaccine Alliance employs innovative finance and the latest technology – from drones to biometrics – to save lives, prevent outbreaks before they can spread and help countries on the road to self-sufficiency. Learn more at www.gavi.org and connect with us on Bluesky , Facebook , Instagram , LinkedIn , TikTok , X and YouTube .
