items.title: Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly plans digital tax collection from night and weekend traders
items.description: The Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly (KMA) is preparing to intensify revenue mobilisation among businesses operating at night and traders who use the Central Business District (CBD) during weekends, as part of efforts to generate additional funds to support sanitation and waste management. The Assembly plans to deploy Point of Sale (POS) devices to facilitate the collection of taxes from night-time businesses, whose trading activities contribute to the accumulation of refuse in the city’s commercial centre. Director of Finance at the KMA, Dr Daniels Owusu, said the initiative was conceived after the Assembly identified a gap in its revenue collection system, with businesses operating beyond regular working hours not contributing adequately to the cost of maintaining the trading environment. In an interview on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, he explained that the Assembly had recognised the need to extend its revenue mobilisation efforts to cover commercial activities taking place at night. “We realised most people worked at night. In Ghana and in the Assembly’s by-laws, any activity you undertake that brings you profit, you have to pay a tax on that. So we decided to see to it that we were taking those taxes,” he stated. Dr Owusu said the decision was also informed by the sanitation challenges associated with night-time trading, particularly in the CBD, where traders generate considerable amounts of waste that must be cleared by the Assembly’s sanitation workers the following morning. He argued that it was unfair for the Assembly to rely solely on revenue collected during the day to finance waste management services that also benefit businesses operating at night. “We realised that, in the night, people continue to do business at the Central Business District (CBD) and they create a lot of refuse which they leave for us to sweep and collect to the landfill site in the morning,” he said. He added that the absence of a corresponding revenue collection system for these businesses meant that the Assembly was bearing the cost of clearing waste generated by traders who did not contribute to the process. “The night traders don’t pay anything to the Assembly and we use the money collected during the day to collect their refuse, so we are going to implement the night collection using POS devices so that we can get enough money for the clearing of the CBD,” he disclosed. Weekend traders also targeted Beyond businesses operating at night, the Assembly is extending its revenue mobilisation plans to traders who conduct business in the CBD during weekends. Dr Owusu said the Assembly had observed that commercial activities continued in the area on Saturdays and Sundays, resulting in additional waste that required cleaning and disposal. He explained that weekend traders had also been included in the proposed collection arrangements to ensure that businesses contributing to the sanitation burden also contribute towards maintaining the area. “In addition, there are a lot of traders who come and do business at the CBD during the weekend and they too create a lot of refuse, so we have targeted them for collection at the weekend,” he stated. The proposed measures are expected to broaden the Assembly’s revenue base and provide additional resources for sanitation operations, particularly in the busy commercial areas of Kumasi. KMA suspends initial implementation after resistance Dr Owusu disclosed that the Assembly had previously commenced the initiative but was forced to suspend its implementation after encountering resistance from some traders and confrontations involving revenue collectors. He said the difficulties arose partly because the initiative was unfamiliar to traders, some of whom suspected that the individuals collecting the taxes were attempting to extort money from them. “We started some months ago but we had challenges. When we started, people thought those collecting the taxes were thieves. It got to a point where the workers fought with the tax collectors. I assume it’s because it was a new initiative,” he explained. According to him, the Assembly had made announcements ahead of the commencement of the exercise to inform traders about the new collection arrangements. However, the initial resistance persisted, compelling management to put the exercise on hold to review its approach and develop strategies for a more effective implementation. Dr Owusu said the Assembly had taken the challenges in good faith and was working towards addressing the concerns that emerged during the initial rollout. He expressed confidence that the initiative could be implemented successfully if existing laws and by-laws governing business taxation were properly enforced. Digital revenue collection boosts KMA mobilisation by 300% Meanwhile, Dr Owusu disclosed that the Assembly’s transition to a digital revenue collection system had significantly improved its revenue mobilisation, recording an increase of about 300 per cent. He cited collections at the Race Course area as an example of the gains achieved since the introduction of the digital system. According to him, the Assembly previously collected approximately GH¢6,000 daily from the area under the former system but now records an average of GH¢18,000 a day. “We were collecting GH¢6,000 a day at Race Course, but we are collecting an average of GH¢18,000 a day. Even on Mondays and Fridays, we are able to collect GH¢22,000 a day, sometimes GH¢16,000, and that’s why we average it at GH¢18,000 a day,” he said. The figures, he noted, demonstrate the potential of digital systems to improve revenue accountability and strengthen the Assembly’s capacity to mobilise funds from commercial activities. The planned deployment of POS devices for night-time and weekend collections is expected to build on these gains by bringing businesses previously outside the Assembly’s regular collection arrangements into the revenue mobilisation framework. The Assembly’s broader objective is to ensure that businesses operating within the metropolis contribute towards the services required to maintain the commercial environment, particularly sanitation and waste disposal.

items.title: DR Congo: Direct Relief Delivers 53 Tons of Medical Aid to Combat Record DRC Ebola Outbreak
items.description: Countries: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Congo, Kenya, Nigeria, South Sudan, Uganda Source: Direct Relief With more than 11,000 confirmed cases reported by the World Health Organization, insecurity in Ituri and North Kivu continues to challenge containment efforts. Direct Relief has provided PPE, diagnostic tools, and chronic care medications across Congo, Uganda, and South Sudan to local health organizations on the front lines. By Noah Smith An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has killed 5,630 people and seen 11,504 confirmed cases, according to the World Health Organization’s Nov. 16 update. Children account for more than a quarter of confirmed cases and one-third of deaths. Seven in 10 children under 5 with confirmed Ebola have died, according to WHO. The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which no vaccines are currently licensed. Declared in May, this is the deadliest outbreak in the country’s history. WHO said Tuesday that 400 to 500 new cases continue to be reported weekly, despite progress in slowing transmission in several early outbreak epicenters. Ituri province remains the outbreak’s epicenter, although transmission has also spread through neighboring North Kivu and other provinces. Insecurity has increasingly disrupted containment efforts. An attack on Cantine-Aloya in North Kivu earlier this month killed 66 civilians, including three health workers, according to WHO. Health facilities were looted and burned, and more than 1,000 contacts of Ebola patients were lost to follow-up. WHO said on Nov. 17 that about two in every three confirmed Ebola deaths occur outside treatment centers. The agency said that points to delays in identifying infections. Direct Relief has delivered 53 tons of Ebola-specific medical aid valued at approximately $15 million to partners in Congo, Uganda and South Sudan as of Nov. 5, including more than 425,000 items of personal protective equipment. Since May 1, Direct Relief has shipped about $47.3 million in medical aid overall to countries affected by the Ebola outbreak . The outbreak has also disrupted routine care for people with other illnesses. The assistance from Direct Relief includes: Essential medicines, intravenous fluids, antibiotics, diagnostic supplies and medications for chronic conditions, helping health facilities maintain routine services while responding to Ebola. A 10-ton shipment containing more than $490,000 in essential medicines, medical supplies and protective equipment arrived in Kinshasa on Nov. 2 for VillageReach , with supplies designated for health facilities in Ituri, Tshopo and Haut-Uele provinces. Direct Relief has also supported Première Urgence Internationale with medical supplies and protective equipment for health facilities in Ituri. The organization provided a $50,000 emergency grant to Humanitarian Action for Africa to strengthen Ebola preparedness in North and South Kivu, including disease surveillance, case management, medical supply management, and community outreach. Last week, Direct Relief shipped approximately 3,800 pounds of protective equipment to the International Organization for Migration in Congo . The shipment included approximately 4,500 protective coveralls and more than 15,000 N95 respirators to support health screenings and disease surveillance along transit routes, at border crossings and in displacement sites. Other partners include Jericho Road, Mulago National Referral Hospital in Uganda, and Association des Diabétiques (Diabetic Association) . Vaccine Research and Regional Risks The WHO said that it expects two vaccine candidates designed for the Bundibugyo virus to join an ongoing trial in Congo in the coming weeks. The trial began in October with Ervebo, a vaccine licensed against a different virus that causes Ebola. Separately, more than 900 people have enrolled in studies of potential treatments. Outside Congo, Kenya has reported nine cases and two deaths, while Nigeria recorded one imported case. Kenya’s last patient has been discharged, and Nigeria’s patient has recovered. Despite expanded laboratory capacity and nearly 2,000 treatment beds, continued transmission and limited access to affected communities remain significant challenges. Health organizations are working to strengthen infection prevention and clinical care while maintaining essential medical services in communities affected by the outbreak.

items.title: FIFM : «Cagoules », Mohamed Mouftakir ausculte les violences qui traversent la jeunesse
items.description: Présenté en première mondiale au Festival international du film de Marrakech, Cagoules, nouveau long-métrage de Mohamed Mouftakir, plonge au cœur d’une jeunesse confrontée à la violence, aux addictions, à la marginalisation et aux défaillances de son environnement familial et social. À travers une galerie de personnages et de trajectoires qui se croisent, le réalisateur marocain interroge les mécanismes d’un phénomène qui surgit parfois brutalement sous les yeux d’une société qui n’a pas toujours su le prévenir. Le nouveau film de Mohamed Mouftakir s’intéresse à une jeunesse confrontée à des réalités souvent reléguées aux marges : drogues dures et hallucinogènes, bandes de jeunes, vols à main armée, violences organisées ou spontanées, mais aussi ruptures familiales et absence de prise en charge. À travers Cagoules, le réalisateur s’intéresse notamment à ce que l’on pourrait considérer comme le visage sombre d’une partie de la « génération Z ». Pour donner corps à cette réalité, Mohamed Mouftakir s’appuie sur une distribution réunissant notamment Majdouline Idrissi, Aziz Dadas, Fahd Benchemsi, Raouia, Yassine Gali, Yassine Rzouki, Sara Bouaabid, Lahcen Razouki et Youssef Ouzlal. Majdouline Idrissi incarne notamment une femme travaillant dans un milieu nocturne et confrontée à sa propre responsabilité de mère. Son personnage, qui a d’abord considéré son enfant comme une charge, se retrouve progressivement rattrapé par le lien maternel. L’une des particularités du film tient justement à son refus de résoudre les situations qu’il met en scène. Mouftakir ne cherche pas à transformer Cagoules en démonstration ou en leçon de morale. Il met plutôt en lumière des symptômes qui, selon lui, gagnent progressivement le corps social avant d’être véritablement pris en considération. À l’issue de la projection, le réalisateur marocain est revenu avec son équipe sur la genèse et les choix artistiques du film. Mohamed Mouftakir, déjà connu pour des œuvres comme Pégase ou Le Chœur des aveugles, explique avoir voulu explorer de nouvelles voies avec Kagoul. « Je teste de nouvelles esthétiques, de nouvelles formes créatives » , a-t-il expliqué, tout en soulignant la continuité d’un thème qui traverse une grande partie de son œuvre : la relation entre le père et le fils. Cette question, précise-t-il, l’accompagne depuis ses premiers films, y compris ses courts-métrages. Elle trouve ici une nouvelle expression, confrontée à un contexte social beaucoup plus violent. Face au public du FIFM, Mouftakir a également insisté sur la dimension collective de la réalisation. « C’est vraiment un effort collectif » , a-t-il déclaré, avant d’ajouter avec une pointe d’autodérision : si le film est réussi, le mérite revient à toute l’équipe ; s’il ne l’est pas, « c’est moi le responsable ». Une manière de rappeler que derrière le regard du réalisateur se trouvent des comédiens, des techniciens, des musiciens et l’ensemble des collaborateurs qui participent à donner une forme à l’œuvre. The post FIFM : «Cagoules », Mohamed Mouftakir ausculte les violences qui traversent la jeunesse appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: TPI de Siguiri : 11 femmes, dont des Sierra-Léonaises, condamnées pour exploitation illégale de l’or et dégradation de l’environnement
items.description: Le verdict est tombé ce lundi 23 novembre 2026 au tribunal de première instance (TPI) de Siguiri. Onze femmes, dont des Sierra-Léonaises, poursuivies pour exploitation illégale de l’or et dégradation de l’environnement, ont été condamnées. Chacune a écopé d’un an d’emprisonnement assorti de sursis et du paiement d’une amende de 3 millions de francs guinéens. Interpellées le 17 novembre dernier dans différentes zones minières, ces prévenues avaient été placées en détention à la maison d’arrêt de Siguiri, dans le cadre des mesures préventives prises par les autorités pour mettre fin à l’exploitation artisanale de l’or sur les sites concernés de la région administrative de Siguiri. Lors de leur comparution devant le juge audiencier, ces onze femmes ont toutes reconnu les faits qui leur sont reprochés. Au cours des débats, certaines ont évoqué leur statut de veuves et expliqué que l’exploitation minière constituait pour elles un moyen de subvenir aux besoins alimentaires de leurs enfants et de leurs familles. D’autres ont également mis en avant les difficultés financières et la précarité dans lesquelles elles vivent. Dans ses réquisitions, le ministère public, représenté par le substitut du procureur de la République près le tribunal de première instance de Siguiri, Simon Pierre Milimono, a demandé au tribunal de retenir ces femmes dans les liens de la prévention et de les condamner à deux ans d’emprisonnement assortis de sursis et au paiement d’une amende de 3 millions de francs guinéens chacune. Après examen du dossier et des débats à l’audience, le tribunal, présidé par Aboubacar 3 Barry, a finalement prononcé contre chacune des onze femmes une peine d’un an d’emprisonnement avec sursis, assortie du paiement d’une amende de 3 millions de francs guinéens. Nouhan Konaté, correspondant régional basé à Siguiri L’article TPI de Siguiri : 11 femmes, dont des Sierra-Léonaises, condamnées pour exploitation illégale de l’or et dégradation de l’environnement est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Une rencontre peut en cacher une autre : Quand le tête-à-tête des trois grandes puissances éclipse les 21 membres au sommet de l'APEC
items.description: La rencontre entre Xi Jinping, Vladimir Poutine et Donald Trump, organisée en marge du sommet de l'APEC à Shenzhen, a capté l'essentiel de l'attention. Au-delà de son caractère historique, ce tête-à-tête de moins de deux heures a donné à voir les rapports de force entre les trois grandes puissances, leurs ambitions respectives et la place qu'elles entendent occuper sur l'échiquier mondial. Une séquence diplomatique qui a relégué au second plan les échanges entre les 21 membres de l'organisation. Du 18 au 19 novembre 2026, s'est tenu à Shenzhen, en Chine, le sommet de l'APEC 2026, marqué notamment par une rencontre de moins de deux heures entre les présidents chinois, russe et américain. Pourquoi une rencontre entre les trois plus grandes puissances militaires du monde suscite-t-elle autant d'inquiétudes chez les absents ? Pas chez tous, car l'Afrique et l'Europe, les grandes absentes de cette rencontre Asie-Pacifique, ne réagissent pas avec la même intensité. Comment expliquer qu'un sommet régional suscite autant d'appréhensions en Europe, qui y voit les prémices d'un nouveau partage du monde ? Si l'Europe, et particulièrement l'Ukraine, en guerre contre la Russie, dénonce le risque que des décisions soient prises sans elle, l'Afrique, quant à elle, ne semble guère se sentir concernée par cette rencontre. La plupart des pays africains préfèrent confier leur sort à des tuteurs, convaincus que la protection d'une puissance extérieure peut les mettre à l'abri et que la natte des autres est toujours meilleure. Que retenir de cette rencontre entre les dirigeants de la région Asie-Pacifique, qui a l'avantage de réunir les trois pays disposant du plus grand nombre d'ogives nucléaires, à savoir les États-Unis, la Russie et la Chine ? Pourquoi trois dirigeants de l'APEC ont-ils relégué au second plan une rencontre réunissant 21 membres ? L'organisation régionale de l'Asie-Pacifique remonte à 1989, à la suite d'une initiative du Premier ministre australien de l'époque, Bob Hawke. Composée de 12 pays à sa création, l'Agence de coopération économique Asie-Pacifique compte aujourd'hui 21 membres « qui représentent plus de 60 % du PIB mondial et près de 2,7 milliards d'habitants (soit 40 % de la population du globe). » L'APEC est une organisation multilatérale qui promeut le libre-échange et privilégie la recherche du consensus lors de ses rencontres. Toutefois, les décisions qui y sont prises ne sont pas contraignantes. Les dirigeants des entreprises des pays membres participent également à ces rencontres. L'APEC est la seule organisation qui réunit en son sein les trois grandes puissances mondiales que sont les États-Unis, la Chine et la Russie. Elle regroupe également des puissances moyennes comme le Japon, le Canada, la Corée du Sud, l'Australie, la Nouvelle-Zélande et Taïwan. Géographiquement, l'Inde pourrait en faire partie, mais certains pays s'y opposent au motif qu'elle n'aurait pas entrepris certaines réformes économiques. Jusqu'ici, l'APEC tenait ses réunions annuelles sans que celles-ci n'attirent particulièrement l'attention des médias du monde entier. Mais cette année, la Chine accueille le sommet et son président, Xi Jinping, a voulu, pour la première fois, réunir à Shenzhen des dirigeants de premier plan. Cette technopole futuriste du pays se distingue par ses voitures autonomes qui circulent dans les rues, ses drones qui sillonnent le ciel et ses robots qui travaillent dans les usines ou servent le café au centre de conférences, le tout dans un paysage urbain dominé par de nombreux gratte-ciel. La région Asie-Pacifique est particulièrement touchée par le blocage du détroit d'Ormuz. Le coût de l'énergie constitue, par ailleurs, une préoccupation majeure pour toutes les économies. Dans ce contexte, on pourrait penser que la fin de la guerre en Iran aurait dû être abordée. Les États-Unis sont le pays qui a déclenché la guerre contre l'Iran. La Russie et la Chine, quant à elles, sont des alliées de l'Iran. Pourtant, cette question sensible n'a figuré ni à l'ordre du jour de la rencontre entre les trois grandes puissances ni à celui des autres échanges. Dans le communiqué final, il est question de la paix dans le monde, sans qu'il soit fait mention de la guerre en Ukraine. Pourquoi les dirigeants de la Russie, de la Chine et des États-Unis se sont-ils retrouvés pendant un peu plus d'une heure ? Cette rencontre est historique, puisqu'il s'agit d'une première. Mais chacun des dirigeants est venu pour montrer au monde sa place et sa puissance, tout en rappelant à ses soutiens qu'il compte toujours sur l'échiquier mondial. Commençons par la Russie, qui figurait sur la photo de Yalta. À l'époque, elle ne s'appelait pas Fédération de Russie, mais Union des républiques socialistes soviétiques (URSS). Grande gagnante de la Seconde Guerre mondiale, elle était devenue une puissance contrôlant plus de la moitié de l'Europe. Aujourd'hui, la Fédération de Russie est en guerre contre l'un de ses voisins, l'Ukraine, un ancien pays de l'URSS désormais soutenu par l'Europe et en partie abandonné par les États-Unis de Donald Trump, même si ce désengagement n'est pas encore total. Les États-Unis sont également en guerre contre l'Iran, mais ne parviennent pas à le vaincre. Quant à Donald Trump, il vient de subir un revers électoral, les Républicains ayant essuyé une défaite lors des élections des deux chambres du Parlement de son pays. Le sommet de Shenzhen, vitrine du spectacle de la puissance chinoise Pour ces deux dirigeants, le sommet constitue une parenthèse au cours de laquelle ils peuvent encore apparaître comme des maîtres du monde. La Russie occupe la deuxième place sur le plan militaire, notamment grâce à son arsenal nucléaire, derrière les États-Unis. Ces derniers restent en tête sur les plans militaire, économique et technologique, mais peut-être plus pour longtemps. Dans cette course, ils avancent en gardant un œil sur la Chine, qui est désormais sur leurs talons et menace de les dépasser. Ils ne peuvent, dès lors, que tenter de retarder cette échéance, notamment en refusant de lui vendre les puces Nvidia destinées aux ordinateurs des centres de données et aux applications d'intelligence artificielle. L'économie américaine ne conserve son avance que grâce à l'intelligence artificielle, tandis que la Chine dispose des terres rares comme d'un atout stratégique pour la contrer et la rattraper. S'il fallait désigner un gagnant de cette rencontre, ce serait Xi Jinping, l'hôte du sommet. À travers le protocole réservé à ses invités, il a clairement montré le rang qu'il accordait à chacun. Il a accueilli Donald Trump à la passerelle de son avion, mais ne s'est pas déplacé pour recevoir Vladimir Poutine. Ce dernier a pourtant grandement besoin de Xi Jinping et de son pays pour contourner les sanctions qui le frappent, notamment grâce aux achats de pétrole et au soutien apporté à son effort de guerre. Le dirigeant chinois semble ménager Donald Trump, qui dispose encore de deux années au pouvoir, même si sa position est affaiblie par le résultat des élections de mi-mandat. Cela pourrait éviter une reprise de la guerre des tarifs douaniers et maintenir seulement dans les journaux cette affaire d'espionnage sexuel de Nvidia. La Chine affirme également sa puissance dans la région Asie-Pacifique en plaçant le Premier ministre japonais en bout de table lors du dîner, comme si par ce geste, l'ancien colonisé voulait exprimer son ressentiment. Ces trois pays, la Chine, les États-Unis et la Russie, sont des puissances qui cherchent à étendre leur influence, car leurs dirigeants et leurs idéologues continuent de raisonner en termes de zones d'influence, même si aucun partage du monde comparable à celui de Yalta n'a été officiellement établi. La Russie se verrait bien en maîtresse de l'Europe et de l'Afrique, la Chine en puissance dominante de l'Asie et du Pacifique, et les États-Unis en maîtres du continent américain. Toutefois, certaines régions ne se prêtent pas à une entente durable entre ces puissances, car la recherche du profit nourrit les rivalités et les confrontations. La Chine a notamment besoin de l'Europe, de l'Amérique du Sud et de l'Afrique pour écouler sa production industrielle. Le sommet réunissant les présidents chinois, russe et américain aura donc permis de montrer la grandeur de la Chine et son président. Xi Jinping, en ressort comme un dirigeant sur lequel on peut compter, qui ne part pas en guerre sur un coup de tête et privilégie le multilatéralisme, contrairement à ses deux hôtes. Sana Guy Lefaso.net

items.title: Sénégal : Macky Sall ferme la porte à l’OIF et revendique son engagement politique
items.description: L'ancien president senegalais Macky Sall n'envisage pas d'etre candidat a la presidence de l'Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF). Dans un entretien accorde a Jeune Afrique , et publie le 23 novembre, il affirme que cette perspective ne l'interesse pas, precisant que seule une responsabilite aux Nations unies aurait pu retenir son attention. « Je suis un homme politique », souligne-t-il, alors qu'il reste engage dans la vie politique senegalaise malgre son installation a Marrakech, au Maroc, depuis avril 2024. Son retrait de la course au poste de secretaire general de l'ONU, en octobre dernier, ne signifie donc pas qu'il entend mettre un terme a ses activites politiques. Macky Sall entend rester a la tete de l'APR Macky Sall entend egalement conserver la direction de l'Alliance pour la Republique (APR), le parti qu'il a fonde et dirige avant son depart du pouvoir en 2024. Il affirme rester en contact regulier avec les responsables de la formation et ne voit pas la necessite de mettre en place une direction provisoire ou un college charge de le remplacer. L'ancien chef de l'etat senegalais ecarte ainsi l'hypothese d'un passage de relais a la tete du parti, malgre son absence du Senegal et les departs de certains responsables. Il se montre egalement reserve sur la perspective d'une alliance avec le mouvement Kiiraay-Les Patriotes republicains. Cette position intervient alors que l'APR traverse une periode de recomposition depuis la defaite electorale de 2024 et l'arrivee au pouvoir de Bassirou Diomaye Faye. Des echanges limites avec son successeur Interroge sur ses rapports avec le president Bassirou Diomaye Faye, Macky Sall evoque notamment leur rencontre de juillet dernier. Selon lui, leurs echanges ont principalement porte sur sa candidature au poste de secretaire general des Nations unies, et non sur la situation politique interieure du Senegal. Il aborde egalement les tensions entre le chef de l'etat et son ancien Premier ministre, Ousmane Sonko, notamment autour du budget et des relations avec l'Assemblee nationale. Sans annoncer de demarche particuliere, l'ancien president reste attentif a l'evolution de la situation politique dans le pays. La presidentielle de 2029 en pointille La question d'un retour de Macky Sall sur la scene politique senegalaise, a l'approche de l'election presidentielle de 2029, reste ouverte. Certains responsables de l'APR souhaitent son retour au Senegal et le voient comme une figure centrale de la strategie du parti. L'ancien president ne confirme toutefois pas de candidature pour le prochain scrutin. Il laisse ainsi planer l'incertitude sur ses intentions electorales, tout en reaffirmant sa volonte de conserver la maîtrise de sa formation politique.

items.title: 21-year-old man jailed for 4 years for assaulting firefighter at Yvonne Okoro’s residence
items.description: The Achimota Circuit Court has sentenced Sampson Azumah to four years’ imprisonment with hard labour for assaulting a firefighter who responded to an emergency at the residence of actress Yvonne Okoro at Adjiringanor in November 2025. Azumah was convicted of unlawfully causing harm to the fire officer after an incident in which personnel of the Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) were reportedly attacked while attending to an emergency at the actress’s residence. The court, presided over by Justice Akosua Anokyewaa Adjepong, found Azumah guilty of the offence and sentenced him to 48 months’ imprisonment with hard labour. The incident occurred in November 2025 when fire officers were dispatched to the residence following an emergency call. During the operation, Azumah allegedly attacked one of the responding officers with a screwdriver after the firefighter sprinkled water on him. The assault occurred while the personnel were carrying out their emergency response duties, raising concerns about the safety of firefighters who routinely put themselves in danger to protect lives and property. Reacting to the court’s decision in an interview with JoyNews’ Fatawu Bayaga, the Greater Accra Regional Commander of the GNFS, Rashid Kwame Nisawu, described the conviction as a significant victory for the Service and its personnel. He urged firefighters not to be discouraged by attacks in the line of duty, stressing that their responsibility required them to move towards danger to rescue people and protect property. “To my fire officers, I think today is a victory. Nobody should be discouraged. We have signed on to a job that when others are running away, we are running in to save lives and property, and I think we’ll continue to do that. “To the Chief Fire Officer, we thank her so much because she encourages us to ensure that this case gets to a fair conclusion today. To the Ghana Police Service, we thank them so much. If not for their prosecution, we wouldn’t have gotten to where we are. “But to other like-minded criminals, this is the first step. Anybody who dares the fire officer is going to end up this way. Even worse punishment than this, I can assure you,” he said. Mr Nisawu also expressed gratitude to the Chief Fire Officer for her encouragement and support in ensuring that the case proceeded to a conclusion. He commended the Ghana Police Service for its role in prosecuting the matter, saying its efforts had been instrumental in securing the conviction. The regional commander further warned individuals who might consider attacking firefighters that such conduct would attract serious consequences, describing the sentence as an important step towards protecting emergency responders. He maintained that the ruling should serve as encouragement to fire personnel to remain committed to their duties, regardless of the dangers they encounter while responding to emergencies.

items.title: Ablakwa confirms return of Ghanaian woman assaulted by employer in Iraq
items.description: The Government of Ghana has located a Ghanaian woman who featured in a viral video showing her being subjected to a violent and dehumanising assault by her employer in Iraq. Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa confirmed that the woman had escaped from her attackers and returned to Ghana with the help of her family, following efforts to establish her whereabouts after the disturbing footage went viral on social media. In a social media post on November 24, Ablakwa expressed relief at the development, announcing that he had met the woman and her family to hear an account of her experience. “Glad to disclose that we found our compatriot in that awfully distressing viral video from Iraq,” he stated. The Minister disclosed that the woman, Stephanie Nkrumah, had successfully escaped from her attackers and returned to Ghana before the meeting with the government. During the meeting, officials listened to the woman’s account of her ordeal and encouraged her to provide information about those allegedly responsible for the assault. According to the Minister, details about her alleged abusers and their network would assist the government in its diplomatic efforts to pursue justice. “We listened carefully to her narrate her ordeal and encouraged her to share with us details of her abusers and their network to assist us in our diplomatic efforts for justice,” he said. The Minister also confirmed that Ghana had formally protested to Iraqi authorities, demanding appropriate action in response to the assault. Government pledges support for recovery Beyond efforts to pursue accountability, the government has also committed to supporting the woman as she recovers from the experience. Following a medical assessment, the government is providing urgent medical care at no cost, alongside clinical psychological support, in line with doctors’ recommendations. The Minister also disclosed that he had donated GH¢50,000 to her as initial financial assistance towards establishing a small business. In addition, he pledged to offer her a scholarship to enable her resume her formal education, which she discontinued some years ago. The support, according to the Minister, is intended to help her rebuild her life following the traumatic experience. He reaffirmed the government’s commitment to protecting the welfare and dignity of Ghanaians living and working abroad, stressing that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and its diplomatic missions would continue to prioritise their safety. Emphasising the government’s position, he said: “As I keep insisting, an attack on any Ghanaian out there, is an attack on all of us.” He further assured the woman of the government’s continued backing as she pursues justice and begins her recovery.

items.title: Freedom of speech should not become a shield for those crossing 'red lines', says Naqvi
items.description: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Tuesday asserted that freedom of speech should not become a shield for those who cross “red lines”. He made the remarks while addressing a seminar organised by the Sustainable Development Policy Institute (SDPI). At the outset of his speech, the minister said that there were four “red lines” for the state: terrorism, hate speech, incitement to violence and sexual exploitation of children. “On these four points, there is no compromise. Pakistan has paid for terrorism in blood. As interior minister, I have attended the funerals of martyrs. And very often, the hate that killed them began on a mobile phone,” he said. He alleged that only 47 per cent of the complaints made by the Counter Terrorism Department were acted upon by social media platforms. “This is not about technology, this is about people. We are not saying that free speech must be curtailed […] journalists must report, citizens must question, dissent must be heard, including against the government, but freedom of speech can never become a shield for those who cross these red lines,” he said. He went on to say that Pakistan had “limited manpower”, resources and technology. Giving the example of Punjab, he said that the province had a population of 140 million against a strength of 61 people in the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA). “And these 61 people include drivers, clerks and officers. We cannot do this alone. That is why we have established a Social Media Protection Regulatory Authority,” he said. The minister called for moving from policy towards enforcement. “To begin with [social media] platforms, OTT services and major content creators must register with the authority. Registration is not a licence to silence anyone, it tells us who is accountable when something goes wrong,” he said. He said that every social media platform “must name an empowered representative for Pakistan, who can actually take decisions”. “Similarly, citizens need one complaint channel they can track. We are moving all NCCIA complaints onto the Pak ID app and the authority is building a single fully tracked complaint system,” he said. Naqvi then went on to recount a recent town hall meeting, where he met five girls who were on the verge of ending their lives due to someone about to release “sensitive material” on social media platforms. “We don’t have any pathway for approaching those platforms. It’s their responsibility to react immediately to save these innocent lives,” he said. The minister said that the social media authority would verify whether action had been taken or not. “Finally, enforcement will be step by step: engagement, then notice, then penalties. Blocking a whole [social media] platform will remain a last resort … our request will be clear, lawful and open to review,” he said. “The state should not feel helpless. Yet, we see terrorist groups still recruiting, still raising terrorist funds, still spreading fear on these very platforms,” he said. Giving an example, Naqvi said that the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) was a declared terrorist organisation, yet “many of their officials are still using these platforms”. “If it is a declared [terrorist] organisation, then who allows them to move around and use all these platforms? Someone needs to stop [them]. This is our request,” he said. “If you are not doing it, what meaning should we take? If it is declared by your country that this organisation is a blacklisted organisation, is a terrorist organisation and then you don’t take action, there’s a big question mark,” he said. He added that the government was focusing on the capacity building of the NCCIA. “Today, I extend an open hand to all these platforms. Let us sit together, not across the table. Operate globally, be accountable globally and never let Pakistani citizens feel unheard,” he concluded.

items.title: Academically advanced pupils should be allowed to sit BECE early– Dr Tutu-Boahene
items.description: A Lecturer in Political Marketing at the University of Education, Winneba (UEW), Dr Bernard Tutu-Boahene, has questioned the rationale behind restricting academically advanced pupils from sitting the Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE) before their designated examination year. He argues that pupils develop intellectually and attain maturity at different rates, making it necessary for education authorities to consider individual academic abilities rather than insist that all children follow the same educational timeline. Speaking on JoyNews’ AM Show on Tuesday, 24 November, Dr Tutu-Boahene said differences in intelligence and maturity meant some pupils could acquire the requisite knowledge and demonstrate the ability to undertake the examination earlier than others. His comments come in the wake of a directive by the Minister for Education, Haruna Iddrisu, instructing the Ghana Education Service (GES) to impose a two-year examination ban on pupils who attempt to sit the BECE before their designated examination year. The directive has sparked renewed debate about whether pupils who demonstrate exceptional academic ability should be allowed to advance ahead of the conventional three-year junior high school (JHS) period. Dr Tutu-Boahene, drawing on his understanding of educational psychology, maintained that children could perform remarkably well academically when given the right guidance and learning environment. “One of the critical things that I’ve learnt from educational psychology is this: when children are young and they pursue educational prospects, because they are not exposed, they concentrate on education, and most of them do well with proper guidance,” he said. He questioned the justification for compelling academically capable pupils to complete the entire three-year JHS programme before being allowed to sit the national examination, particularly when some pupils fail despite spending the prescribed period in school. “There are situations where people go into the full length of the so-called three years at the basic level and still don’t pass,” he observed. Against this backdrop, he argued that pupils who could demonstrate the necessary academic competence in JHS One or Two should not automatically be prevented from taking the examination simply because they had not completed the conventional period. “So, if a pupil is capable of sitting the examination in JHS One or Two, why insist that they must go through the entire three-year period?” he questioned. READ ALSO : Early BECE candidates to face two-year examination ban – Education Minister Expanding his argument, Dr Tutu-Boahene said intellectual ability and maturity were not uniform among children, making it inappropriate to assume that all pupils would be ready for academic progression at the same age. He stressed that differences in intelligence quotient (IQ) and individual development could influence how quickly children understood concepts, acquired knowledge and demonstrated their abilities. “Remember that IQs differ. Remember that maturity rates differ,” he said. To illustrate his point, the lecturer explained that some children could demonstrate exceptional abilities at a relatively young age, including performing tasks or engaging in intellectual discussions that might challenge considerably older individuals. For him, these differences reinforce the need to recognise that maturity is an individual process, with some people attaining certain developmental milestones earlier than others.

items.title: Cedi weakens marginally against US dollar, going for GH¢12.45 at forex bureaus, GH¢11.85 in interbank market
items.description: The Ghana cedi has drifted towards its year-to-date weak point of GH¢11.85 in the interbank market as the yuletide season gathers momentum. In the retail market, it is going for GH¢12.45 to one US dollar. The cedi recorded mixed performance across the interbank and retail markets by the close of trading last week. In the interbank market, it depreciated by 0.93% against the American greenback to close trading at GH¢11.80 (average). However, it appreciated by 1.42% and 1.05% against the pound and euro, respectively, to close trading at GH¢15.46 and GH¢12.96, respectively. In parallel, it closed trading at an average of GH¢12.35 to one US dollar in the retail market. This is about a 2.23% depreciation rate. For the pound and euro, it sold at GH¢15.95 per pound (+0.31%) and GH¢13.38 per euro (+1.68%). Contrary to expectations, the cedi closed marginally weaker against the US dollar, as anticipated forex supply from the GoldBod fell short of expectations. “The subdued support over the past two weeks has fuelled dollar demand, pushing US dollar/Ghana cedi closer to its year-to-date high of GH¢11.85 [interbank market]”, Databank Research said. “Looking ahead, we expect further nominal cedi weakness if support from the GoldBod and the Bank of Ghana remains lacklustre amid mounting seasonal dollar demand”, it added. Meanwhile, the cedi began the week, losing value marginally against the dollar. It is presently going for about GH¢12.45 per the US dollar at the forex bureaus.

items.title: Road closures around Karachi’s PIDC junction cause traffic congestion
items.description: KARACHI: Commuters in Karachi’s Saddar area faced traffic congestion and inconvenience on Tuesday after authorities closed some roads around the PIDC junction in response to a sit-in call by the Sindh Indus Lawyers Forum (SILF). In an alert issued at 1:16pm, Karachi Traffic Police said both roads from PIDC Chowk towards the State Life Building, as well as Dr Ziauddin Ahmed Road, were closed to traffic. As an alternative route, traffic was diverted from PIDC Chowk towards Club Road and from the State Life Building towards Beaumont Road. This screengrab from Google Maps shows traffic near the PIDC junction at around 4:30pm on Nov 24, 2026. According to a statement issued by SILF, lawyers staged a sit-in outside the Sindh High Court. They also staged a rally from Shahrah-i-Liaquat towards CM House through Court Road, Sindh Secretariat Chowk, Sindh Assembly and Aiwan-i-Sadr Road. The forum has put forward 16 demands under the banner of ‘Sindh Demands’, including opposition to the division of Sindh and the construction of Jalalpur Canal. The protest call comes as a debate over a “system reset” in the country has intensified over the past few months. In July, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi stirred a political storm by calling for the creation of new administrative units , arguing that the current system of governance had “collapsed” and needed a “reset”. The PML-N-led federal government has insisted on holding a referendum across the country on the establishment of new provinces or administrative units. However, the suggestion has faced severe backlash from its ally PPP, with party chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari saying that any “forced” attempt to divide provinces, particularly Sindh, could lead to bloodshed. SILF said its demands also include “opposition to constitutional amendments and the proposed amendment”, apparently referring to the 26th and 27th Amendments, though no new amendment has been officially proposed. Moreover, SILF’s demands, according to its statement, include stopping alleged irregularities in the Sindh Public Service Commission and alleged government intervention in lawyers’ bars . “Corporate farming and mining in Karoonjhar mountain should be stopped and political prisoners should be released,” SILF further said. On Sunday, a large number of people from across Sindh took to the streets of Karachi in a rally organised by the Jeay Sindh Rahbar Committee, an alliance of four nationalist parties, to protest against any plan for the creation of new provinces or administrative units in Sindh.

items.title: Budget européen : cinq pays rejettent le projet de Costa, Budapest refuse d’y lier l’aide à Kiev
items.description: Le projet presente le 21 novembre par António Costa, president du Conseil europeen, a fait l'objet d'un refus commun de la Hongrie, de la Slovaquie, de la Tchequie, de la Pologne et de l'Autriche. Les discussions achoppent notamment sur la repartition des credits. Budapest refuse une solidarite imposee Le Premier ministre hongrois Peter Magyar a declare : « Nous ne sommes pas d'accord sur le fait que le financement de l'Ukraine soit lie au budget septennal, non pas par manque de solidarite, car les quatre pays du groupe de Visegrád sont solidaires avec l'Ukraine. Cependant, le budget etant deja tendu, il est inacceptable que la fourniture d'une aide financiere a l'Ukraine devienne egalement une condition obligatoire. » Son homologue slovaque Robert Fico affirme que les cinq dirigeants jugent le texte inacceptable. Le Premier ministre tcheque Andrej Babis demande lui aussi de separer l'aide a Kiev du budget general. Les pays du groupe de Visegrád veulent donner la priorite aux regions defavorisees et a l'agriculture. La Pologne et l'Autriche rejettent egalement le projet. L'aide a Kiev preservee malgre les coupes António Costa a pourtant revu la facture a la baisse. Son projet represente 1 582 milliards d'euros aux prix de 2025, soit 40 milliards de moins que la proposition d'octobre et 180,6 milliards de moins que le texte initial de la Commission. L'enveloppe pouvant atteindre 100 milliards d'euros pour l'Ukraine sur sept ans reste, elle, preservee. Ces concessions n'ont pas rapproche les capitales. Les pressions avaient commence avant cette reunion. Berlin a menace de bloquer le prochain budget si tous les etats ne participaient pas au financement de Kiev , une pression que Robert Fico a qualifiee de chantage. Bruxelles a aussi envisage 45 milliards d'euros de prets supplementaires pour 2027, distincts de l'aide prevue pour 2028-2034. La Slovaquie a deja refuse d'y participer . Un sommet sous la menace du veto Les 26 et 27 novembre, les dirigeants de l'UE tenteront de trouver un compromis. Le futur cadre financier doit etre adopte a l'unanimite : les etats recalcitrants disposent donc d'un moyen de pression. En France, l'election presidentielle pourrait egalement peser sur les negociations. Renaud Labaye, directeur adjoint de campagne de Marine Le Pen, a declare au quotidien Le Monde le 16 novembre : « Si on gagne, 2028 verra la fin de l'aide financiere, y compris via l'Union europeenne. » Bruxelles tente ainsi de garantir des financements a Kiev pour plusieurs annees, au moment ou plusieurs gouvernements refusent de les inscrire dans une obligation budgetaire commune.

items.title: The Big Bang Theory : A Theory
items.description: Sheldon Cooper would want to begin with the numbers, so here they are: In 2026, Americans have spent more than 27.5 billion minutes watching the CBS sitcom he anchors, The Big Bang Theory —making it the year’s most popular streaming show among U.S. adults. (Its only rival? The cartoon Bluey , beloved by kids and grown-ups.) Per numbers gathered by Nielsen and aggregated by the data journalist Daniel Parris, Big Bang has surpassed the viewership of a host of newer and buzzier programs, among them The Pitt , Bridgerton , and Stranger Things —this despite the fact that the series premiered nearly 20 years ago and ended its network run in 2019. The show’s current success, Sheldon might observe, is not a statistical anomaly. On the contrary, the series has regularly featured in Nielsen’s Top 10 streaming rankings for the past three years. This year, though, “the show’s viewership has surged to an all-time high,” Parris noted recently in his Stat Significant newsletter. No bombshell from Love Island USA , it seems, can compete with the charms of a theoretical physicist who has an IQ of 187 and an endless desire to remind you about it. In some ways, Big Bang ’s popularity tracks: Nerds are cool now, you might have heard, and few things prove that point as eloquently as the billions of minutes Americans are spending in the geeky company of Sheldon (played by Jim Parsons), the experimental physicist Leonard Hofstadter (Johnny Galecki), the astrophysicist Rajesh Koothrappali (Kunal Nayyar), and the aerospace engineer Howard Wolowitz (Simon Helberg). In another way, though, the show’s afterlife is curious. Big Bang is notably dated, both in its storylines (see: the advent of Siri) and in its sense of humor (among other things, it has been said to have a woman problem ). And even in this Muskified moment , telegenic nerdiness is not the instant sell that Sheldon et al. might want it to be. Genius is, pretty much by definition, unrelatable. Yet the show serves up storylines about science experiments and string theory and Star Trek ’s Kobayashi Maru . Like a Comic-Con panel with plot points, it features cameos from an array of nerd-world luminaries—Stan Lee, LeVar Burton, Wil Wheaton, Neil deGrasse Tyson, and many more. You might expect a sitcom to amuse you. You might not expect it to do so through assorted jokes about Schrödinger’s cat . But Big Bang ’s singularity ( guess what the show also jokes about) helps explain how a TV series, like Schrödinger’s four-legged thought experiment, can be both long dead and very much alive. Series in motion tend to stay in motion, and Big Bang was big from the beginning: During its initial airing, it was regularly one of the most watched series on network TV. Today, it’s a well-promoted presence on HBO Max. Its scenes are repackaged on TikTok. Its spin-offs— Young Sheldon , Georgie and Mandy’s First Marriage , and Stuart Fails to Save the Universe —double, Parris notes in his analysis, as free advertising for the original show. And Big Bang , given the length of its run, is quite a lot of show: 12 seasons, at roughly 20 episodes each, amounting to—well, I’ll leave the exact math to Sheldon, but many, many hours of autoplay-friendly entertainment. The physics, though—the blunt ubiquities that keep Big Bang ever in the ether—are only part of the equation. The show is one of several vintage sitcoms, among them Friends , Seinfeld , New Girl , and The Office , that have proved steadily popular in the streaming era. They owe at least some of that success to the genre they share. Sitcoms’ most widely disparaged tendencies (predictability, low stakes, high camp) are, for many audiences, their most appealing features. Their anodyne nature offers the very thing that so many modern viewers crave: comfort TV. [ Read: Why you can’t stop streaming Seinfeld. Or Frasier. Or Bones. ] Big Bang —a show that finds Leonard, the most socially aware of the geniuses, telling a joke whose punch line is spherical chickens in a vacuum —might seem to deviate from the sitcom’s standard formulas. Instead, it takes them to their logical extremes. A gang of lovable misfits? Check: Sheldon and his friends are so thoroughly misfit that they find themselves barred from a game of Dungeons & Dragons. Plotlines that find humor in banality? Check: Big Bang devoted an episode to Howard’s engineering of a “zero-gravity waste-disposal system” for astronauts on the International Space Station. Jokes that are sharp but accessible? Check again: Here’s Raj’s reaction to Howard’s creation of an extraterrestrial toilet: “This is an important achievement for two reasons: No. 1—and, of course, No. 2.” The friends regularly tease one another; mockery, in this group, is a love language. But they also support one another, reflexively. After Howard’s space commode has been installed on the ISS, he realizes that he has made a mistake with its specs. The guys rally around him, gathering junk that mimics the equipment on the station and staying up all night to help him correct the error. The scenes that result—think Apollo 13 with pizza boxes and poop jokes—are core to Big Bang ’s appeal: Competence can be its own source of comfort. And when it’s a team effort? The comfort compounds. It’s nice to watch people being good at things. It’s even nicer to watch them being good at things while being good to one another. In this, too, Big Bang adheres to well-worn formulas. Every sitcom, whether its characters are relatives or neighbors or co-workers, will be, to some extent, a show about family. Big Bang ’s variation on the theme—genius, in loco familias —is especially poignant because the family the characters build is so unlikely. These are people who, if they hadn’t found one another, might not have anybody else. Had Friends ’ Monica and Rachel lived across the hall from two guys who weren’t Chandler and Joey, they probably would have befriended the other guys anyway: Whatever the characters’ quirks, socializing came naturally to them. Big Bang ’s foursome, though, are more than mere outliers; they’re also outcasts. The guys spent much of their childhoods being bullied. They grew up with families who may have loved them but who didn’t, and couldn’t, fully understand them. To be exceptionally smart, these characters have learned, is to be perpetually excluded. Their baseline condition is isolation. Friendship is a statistical improbability. But this bleak math, rather than compromising the show’s comforts, amplifies them. It heightens the stakes of the characters’ relationships and makes the community that they find, against the odds, all the more remarkable. The guys may sometimes annoy one another. They occasionally misunderstand one another. Yet their bonds never break. Members of the group—which, over the seasons, expands to include the microbiologist Bernadette Rostenkowski (Melissa Rauch) and the neuroscientist Amy Farrah Fowler (Mayim Bialik)—keep coming back together. And all of them keep choosing one another until, eventually, they no longer need to. The thing about chosen family is that it can keep accruing. In Big Bang ’s pilot episode, Sheldon and Leonard get a random new neighbor, an aspiring actress named Penny (Kaley Cuoco). And Penny, once dumb luck has put her in the path of these geniuses, sets several forces in motion. She is a chemical agent in the guys’ lives, fizzing and sparking and transforming everything in her path. Her influence—her kindness, her wit, her tendency to call everyone “sweetie”—transforms Sheldon and Leonard. It makes them savvier and worldlier than they were before: two men, book-smart and street-stupid, whom Penny’s influence turns wise. Insiders and outsiders, assembling and clashing and learning and growing: Writers might talk about character arcs. Scientists might talk about evolution. In his recently released memoir (titled, aptly, Sitcom ), Chuck Lorre, Big Bang ’s co-creator and executive producer, describes the show’s transformation from its initial premise ( geeks, lol ) into the one that made it to the air. Big Bang ’s early pilot, he writes, lacked depth and warmth. It lacked, crucially, Penny and Raj and Howard. It was coming along at a moment when nerds were gaining cultural cachet; rather than humanizing its geeks, though, it resorted to skewering them. Network executives hated it. But CBS gave Lorre and his co-creator, Bill Prady, an opportunity nearly unheard of in network television: a do-over. They revamped the show to feature four geniuses rather than two. They rewrote the woman-next-door character—who is smarter than she might seem, but neurotypical enough to hear “pi” and think of a baked good—as much more central to the story. The Penny who emerged was also, effectively, a stand-in for the show’s audience. Initially baffled by her wacky new neighbors, she comes to appreciate them and soon enough to love them. She encourages the show’s audience to do the same. [ Read: The (slow, awkward) love song of Sheldon Cooper ] What audiences adore is perhaps best encapsulated by a scene featured in Young Sheldon , Big Bang ’s first spin-off. The show follows Sheldon, age 10, as an up-and-coming genius living in a small town in East Texas. At one point, he is shown rigging a radio to listen to a faraway event that is, for him, the Super Bowl and the Oscars in one: the announcement of the year’s Nobel laureates, live from Stockholm. Giddy, Sheldon invites everyone he knows—his family, his academic mentors, the entire student body of his very large high school—to join him for an early-morning listening party. Nobody shows. Emotions, as Sheldon will readily admit, are not his strong suit. Still, he is crushed. The scene is hard to watch: a kid, abandoned by everyone he knows, in direct violation of the laws of comfort TV. But then the camera cuts away from Sheldon, panning out from East Texas to homes in California and India and Nebraska and to the kids who, in 1990, occupied them: Howard playing video games, Raj studying, Penny asleep in her bed. As Young Sheldon becomes, briefly, Young Howard , Young Raj , and the like—as viewers see Leonard in his room in New Jersey, riveted by the same Nobel broadcast—Diana Ross & the Supremes’ “Someday We’ll Be Together” plays in the background. The montage is treacly, sure. You might see it as evidence of corporate interests at work: an ad for the franchise’s original show, product-placed in the new one. But the scene fits. Family is, in its way, an act of vertical integration—a series of connections that can support all of the people they touch. And Young Sheldon ’s audience, for once, knows something that the genius cannot: Togetherness, for him, is a foregone conclusion. His path will lead him to his people. He is alone for now. But he won’t be for long. ​​When you buy a book using a link on this page, we receive a commission. Thank you for supporting The Atlantic .

items.title: ‘Our History Is Better Than Anybody Else’s’
items.description: F or years now, Donald Trump and the MAGA movement have cast the United States as the heir to and defender of Western civilization. In the second Trump administration, this sort of grandiose rhetoric has increased; the administration presents itself as the lone bulwark against the barbarians at the gates who would annihilate everything good about the world. “Our lineage and our legacy hails back to Athens, to Rome,” Stephen Miller, Trump’s longtime adviser and new chief of staff, said at the funeral for the assassinated conservative activist Charlie Kirk. “Our ancestors built the cities. They produced the art and architecture. They built the industry” that pulled “us out of the caves and the darkness into the light.” Secretary of State Marco Rubio gave a similar speech a month ago, in actual Athens. “The story of our civilization is the greatest story ever known to man. And it began here, with the first men and women of the West,” Rubio announced. “This was the foundation of the Western mind: Our math, our science, our medicine. Our philosophy, ethics, and religion. It paved the way for the Gospel of Jesus Christ to find fertile soil in Europe and flourish into the empire of Christendom.” Certainly one can see the legacy of ancient societies in how we live today—the philosophy of Plato and Aristotle, the many denominations of Christianity descended from its embrace by the Romans, the Romance languages spoken from Santiago to Sambava. The American Founders took inspiration from antiquity, a debt you can see in the mighty structures surrounding the National Mall. Yet what many conservatives describe as Western civilization is not so much a consistent historical fact as an ideological project, one that has long been used to demonstrate the inherent superiority of certain people—white people—in order to legitimize a claim to power and dominance. Europe and the West began to emerge as coherent political identities relatively recently, in the early 17th century; they are not timeless, immutable concepts. [ Adam Serwer: The GOP’s message to immigrants ] Some conservative-media figures have been explicit about what they mean by Western civilization. The right-wing podcaster Matt Walsh described Americans as “the best innovators, lawmakers, scientists, artists, athletes, thinkers, and fighters in the entire world. We’re not a ‘melting pot’ or a mishmash of inferior, squabbling cultures.” If the country could just “evict anti-American invaders,” it could go back to being “an unstoppable force advancing the interests of civilization, without apology.” That apology is the problem: America, and by extension the West, has grown weak because it has stopped asserting its superiority over others as a means of honoring its inheritance. “Over time, we in the West came to feel ashamed of the very things that made us exceptional,” Rubio said, and that shame threatened to condemn Americans to “a future of atrophy and servitude and decline.” This sort of argument plays well at rallies, and conservatives have long been trying to institutionalize and intellectualize it through college curricula. But it is based on an outdated historiography that takes into account neither how these ancient societies saw themselves nor their relationship to the societies around them. It is a bedtime story about being the bestest boys who ever lived—in short, a myth. And at the core of this myth is the idea that human progress is the product of isolation and ethnic homogeneity, rather than a collective endeavor. It is one thing to take inspiration from past societies, and another entirely to claim their accomplishments as your own personal inheritance. This is a race-based argument, as if the accomplishment of a Caesar, an Alexander, or a Napoleon belonging to all white people carries any more weight than the average Eagles fan saying, “We won the Super Bowl.” There is no question that Greek and Roman texts from antiquity—Aristotle’s Poetics , Cicero’s speeches, Sappho’s poetry—are worthy of study. Concepts associated with Western civilization, such as democracy, freedom of speech, religious tolerance, and capitalism, have undoubtedly shaped the modern world. But appreciating the canonical texts of what Rubio and others refer to as Western civilization is not the same as telling the story they want to tell, which is that virtually every human achievement of note was attained by Europeans. T he culprit for the West’s loss of confidence, many conservatives believe, is the “woke” university. Richard Nixon said, “The professors are the enemy,” half a century ago, but educational polarization—the drift of college-educated voters to the left and non-college-educated voters to the right—has lent the critique a new urgency. The former Trump adviser Steve Bannon recently told The Boston Globe that universities were the only reason Democrats are “able to compete with us.” One response is to try to force students to learn a particular version of the story of Western civilization, a version that is not a neutral account of concepts such as capitalism, democracy, and Christianity, but an argument that capitalism, democracy, and Christianity are superior to the heathen cultures of foreign barbarians. Republican legislatures and administrators in states such as Texas and Florida have moved to reorient university curricula toward this vision. The Democrats’ sweep of state offices in Texas may halt some of these changes, but unwinding them will take time, while the general trend in red states is likely to continue. In 2023, Florida Governor Ron DeSantis championed legislation to “ensure Florida’s public universities and colleges are grounded in the history and philosophy of Western Civilization.” William Inboden, the provost at the University of Texas at Austin, has called for a renewed commitment “to the American people, our constitutional order, Western civilization, and the classical liberal arts.” The shift at UT Austin and elsewhere coincided with the slashing of courses related to race and gender—perhaps because these subjects threaten to complicate the preferred narrative of Western civilization. Conservatives have tried to present this effort as “depoliticizing” scholarship, in Inboden’s description. But historians are always making new discoveries or reinterpreting old ones. What these conservatives are really attempting to do is stop the process of revision and rediscovery in favor of past interpretations that promote the idea that America is the successor to the great civilizations of antiquity, and is thus entitled to dominate the world in the name of humanity. “One powerful tool of legitimacy is invoking a past golden age,” the historian Ada Palmer writes in Inventing the Renaissance . “Golden ages are mythical constructions (the events are real but the golden ageness is invented), so it’s easy to claim you are the true successor, even if you have little historical connection.” The question, though, is legitimacy for what? America’s Founders were arguably some of the original Roman-statue guys: Grounding American independence in the Greco-Roman world allowed the colonists to smooth over denominational divides and justify their own freedoms alongside the institution of slavery and the dispossession of Native Americans. John Stuart Mill argued that “despotism is a legitimate mode of government in dealing with barbarians, provided the end be their improvement.” Convenient for the despot! What this narrative misses is the fact that the idea of separate civilizations at all is a relatively young one. In How the World Made the West , the classical historian Josephine Quinn identifies the idea as originating in the 19th century, alongside, not coincidentally, the age of colonization. European nations that sought to subjugate other peoples found it convenient to posit that those peoples were inferior, and that despotism was thus justified. The world was hardly harmonious before that; war and ethnic strife were common. But the concept of civilization was generally thought of as singular, Quinn writes, as in human civilization. The narrative of separate civilizations was later adapted for the Cold War, and revived for the post-9/11 era. Now it has been resurrected as self-soothing rhetoric for a right-wing-populist project, a kind of collectivist monarchist belief that white people—or, in euphemism, “the West”—are born to rule. But we know now that the world of antiquity was much more interconnected than was previously believed. As Quinn writes, human civilization is a story of “exchange between people from different places and cultures,” and “without it there wouldn’t be much of a story at all.” Ancient Greece took inspiration from the Egyptians to its south and the Phoenicians (from whom they drew their alphabet) and Assyrians to its east. The Iliad and The Odyssey , Quinn writes, “show us that Greek speakers of that era still chose to sing of international kingdoms, intercontinental war, and voyages across broad seas.” Greek coins and Roman amphorae have been found in India, where Alexander led his army and where Greek kingdoms existed for centuries afterward. Augustus’s legions marched south along the Nile until halted by the queen of Kush, a kingdom that had been in contact with the Greeks for generations and had provided Egypt with many of its rulers. We do math with Arabic numerals, and the concept of zero was invented by an Indian mathematician in the seventh century. The main religion of Western civilization, Christianity, was founded by an Aramaic-speaking rabbi in West Asia. Agriculture, philosophy, literacy, navigation, metalworking—all of these advanced in antiquity because goods and people traveled, and ideas traveled with them. “What are called Western values—freedom, rationality, justice, and tolerance—are not only or originally western,” Quinn writes, “and the West itself is in large part a product of long-standing links with a much larger network of societies, to south and north as well as east.” I am not arguing that these societies were “superior” to Western ones—only that societies learn from contact with one another rather than through ethnic purity and enforced segregation. Taking the Greeks and Romans as the origin of Western civilization is an ideological project, not a historical one, a little bit like a posthumous baptism. The ancients largely did not see race the way many of our contemporaries do: as an immutable biological category. Projecting that conception backwards is like imagining that Xerxes scrolled through updates on the Battle of Thermopylae on his iPhone. The stereotypes that ancients did embrace rarely line up with contemporary views. Aristotle, for example, did not consider the Greek city-states part of Europe, whose population he dismissed as inferior. People who lived in Europe’s colder regions, he wrote, were “full of spirit but inferior with regard to intelligence and skill,” adding that they lacked “civic organization and the ability to rule their neighbours.” Rome, meanwhile, as the classicist Naoíse Mac Sweeney writes in The West , “ gloried in the idea of itself as a mongrel nation,” tracing its mythical origin, in Virgil’s epic Aeneid , not to Northern Europe, but to Troy, in Asia. As Quinn writes, “As late as the first century BCE some Roman geographers were still unsure whether Europe and Africa were separate continents.” That’s understandable, considering that North African grain kept the empire fed, and “by the 180s CE nearly a third of Roman senators were of African origin.” Basically everyone in the Roman empire was a “polyglot,” Palmer writes. “One heard all sorts of languages in the streets of Rome: Aramaic, Hebrew, etc., with Greek serving as a lingua Franca.” Many of the texts that tell us about these worlds, the supposed blueprints of Western civilization, might have been lost during the Middle Ages, Mac Sweeney points out, if they had not been preserved in places such as the House of Wisdom, the great library in Baghdad that drew scholars from all over the world. C laiming descent from the Roman empire is an ancient, and global, pastime. The citizens of the Eastern Roman empire called themselves Romans, never Byzantines. Once they were defeated by the Ottomans, the sultan took the title kayser-i-rum , or “Caesar of Rome.” The czar of Russia is similarly derived from caesar . Ivan III went so far as to marry the Byzantine princess Sophia Palaiologina to bolster Moscow’s claim to being the “Third Rome.” The Holy Roman Empire put it right there in the name. So many of Trump’s political strategies are intended to make the same case: the “Western civilization” speeches; the landmarks he names after himself; the proposals to colonize Greenland and Canada; the calls for public executions of enemies; the grand ballroom and arch in Washington, D.C. It is a regime legitimization tactic dreamed up by a 10-year-old who wants to grow up to be Roman emperor. [ Listen: Why America isn’t Rome (and why that matters) ] MAGA’s nostalgia for this outdated historiography has been used to back up arguments that demographic change, expansions of civic equality, and political transition threaten the advance of civilization, instead of being the prerequisites for it. Better to throw up walls, tariff your allies and enemies alike, pursue mass deportation, defund and censor scholarship, and wage wars to demonstrate your superior might. In a speech to the Federalist Society this month dismissing the legitimacy of the International Criminal Court, Rubio quoted the Roman general Pompey: “Stop quoting laws to men with swords.” John Adams was fond of quoting a different Roman, Cicero: “ cedant arma togae ,” or “let arms give way to togas.” The Founders idealized the Roman republic —not the Roman empire, which they saw as a cautionary tale about the death of free societies. Pompey’s quote foreshadows that death—and his own beheading. Rubio’s praise for the rule of arms over the rule of law identifies him as the kind of man the Founders thought had destroyed the republic, instead of defending it. Thomas Jefferson called appeals to force like Rubio’s “the vital principle and immediate parent of despotism.” Judging by the results of the midterms, voters don’t see the Trump era as a new golden age. This administration does share some qualities with ancient Rome—a predilection for oligarchy , public executions , and losing wars to Persia , to name just a few. But the idea of America as the apex of civilization will persist long after MAGA is gone, because people’s identities and the status they derive from those identities are important to them. Stories like these stick because they convey a simple message: We are better . Maybe the we is “Americans.” Maybe it’s Europeans. Maybe it’s men, heterosexuals, Christians, or conservatives. As Rubio put it: “I never said our history is perfect. I have only said our history is better than anybody else’s.” But as Quinn writes, civilizations do not advance through isolation; they advance through exchange. There is no ancient Greece without Phoenicia and Mesopotamia, no ancient Rome without Egypt and Anatolia, and, I would add, no America without African gold and labor . Clearly, these exchanges are not always pleasant or mutually beneficial. War, genocide, slavery, and exploitation are cornerstones of the human experience. Antiquity was not a tolerant, multiracial paradise, but neither is the story of humanity a hero’s journey with the Great White Man as protagonist. Given how human civilization actually advances, the fixation on purity and uniformity is self-destructive. Without change, without dynamism, societies are doomed to decay. Rather than preserving “civilization,” you suffocate your own society like a candle flame in a bell jar.

items.title: Labé : une collision entre un camion-remorque et une Renault 21 fait un mort et plusieurs blessés à Popodara
items.description: Un grave accident de la circulation s'est produit dans la soirée du lundi 23 novembre 2026, à Horé Pétéwol, dans la commune rurale de Popodara, préfecture de Labé. Le bilan fait état d'une femme décédée et de plusieurs blessés, dont certains dans un état grave. Selon les informations recueillies, l'accident a impliqué un camion-remorque et un véhicule Renault 21 qui revenait d'un marché hebdomadaire. La victime, identifiée comme Idiatou, était originaire de Honladè, dans la commune rurale de Popodara. Joint par notre correspondant, Maître Diouldé, chargé des conflits et des négociations au sein du syndicat des transporteurs de Popodara, est revenu sur les circonstances du drame. « C'est après la prière de 19 heures que j'ai reçu un appel m'informant qu'un accident venait de se produire à Horé Pétéwol. Il s'agissait d'une collision entre un camion-remorque et un véhicule Renault 21. J'étais alors dans notre parc. Je me suis immédiatement rendu à la gendarmerie pour signaler les faits. Ensuite, nous sommes allés sur les lieux et avons effectivement constaté l'accident », a-t-il expliqué. Poursuivant son témoignage, il a indiqué qu'une femme avait perdu la vie et que plusieurs autres personnes avaient été blessées. Les cas les plus graves ont été évacués à l'hôpital régional de Labé pour y recevoir des soins. « La victime est une femme originaire de Honladè, dans la commune rurale de Popodara. Elle s'appelait Idiatou et était l'épouse de mon grand frère, Monsieur Tala Oury. Je ne connais pas le nombre exact de passagers qui se trouvaient à bord du taxi. C'est un véhicule qui revenait d'un marché hebdomadaire. La victime et le chauffeur sont tous deux originaires de Popodara », a-t-il précisé. Face à ce nouveau drame routier, Maître Diouldé a lancé un appel à la prudence à l'endroit des conducteurs et des transporteurs, les invitant notamment à éviter les excès de vitesse. « Certes, c'est Dieu qui décide de notre sort, mais l'excès de vitesse est également un facteur de risque. Je leur demande donc de rouler doucement pour éviter de tels drames », a-t-il exhorté. La Protection civile, en collaboration avec le syndicat des transporteurs de Popodara, a procédé à la prise en charge des victimes et à leur évacuation vers l'hôpital régional de Labé. Le corps de la défunte a également été transporté à la morgue de cet établissement sanitaire. Au moment où nous mettions cet article en ligne, les agents de police étaient attendus sur les lieux pour effectuer le constat avant le dégagement des deux véhicules et la libération de la chaussée. Alpha Moussa Dieng, correspondant régional à Labé L’article Labé : une collision entre un camion-remorque et une Renault 21 fait un mort et plusieurs blessés à Popodara est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .
